# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group responsible for defining governance standards, risk evaluation frameworks, and regulatory alignment patterns for agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a]. It operates alongside other foundation groups such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group tracks discussions, decisions, deliverables, and action items via standardized meeting templates and agentic workflow conventions[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

Repository operational templates and documentation workflows were established to record recurring working group proceedings[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: The Technical Committee (TC) oversees technical governance, project lifecycles, and working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governance body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for guiding technical vision, managing project lifecycles, and establishing working groups under the authority of the Governing Board [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Specification
## Composition and Operations
The TC assists the Governing Board (GB) by reviewing project proposals, recommending candidate projects, and applying the AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Each Platinum Member of AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the TC [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The TC elects an annual Chair and optional Co-Chair to preside over proceedings.

## Responsibilities
The TC's core responsibilities include [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups across relevant domain areas.
- Coordinating collaboration between Technical Projects and establishing community technical priorities.
- Recommending projects to the GB for acceptance and deciding project lifecycle stage transitions.
- Recommending resource priorities to the GB to support Technical Projects.

## Decision Making and Voting
The TC functions as a consensus-driven body with the following decision mechanisms [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- **Lazy Consensus**: Proposals are automatically approved if no formal objections are lodged within 72 hours.
- **Voting**: Decisions requiring a formal vote operate on a one-vote-per-voting-member basis with a 50% quorum threshold.
- **Objections**: If lazy consensus is broken by an objection, resolution via electronic vote requires approval from a majority of all TC voting members.
- **Escalation**: Unresolved votes may be escalated by any TC member to the Governing Board.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-03**: Technical Committee Charter formally adopted [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative focused on evaluating governance frameworks, risk management standards, and regulatory compliance requirements for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Specification
## Operating Model
The working group operates under pre-competitive collaboration boundaries and submits its charter and 90-day plans to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

## Deliverable Methodology
The working group follows a three-step working model [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Mapping existing standards, sector regulations (e.g., EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, GDPR/PII controls), and industry best practices [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying areas where existing governance frameworks do not address risks unique to autonomous agent interactions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance**: Formulating principles and guidance for organizations deploying agentic architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-19**: Working group kickoff meeting held covering governance, antitrust rules, and regulatory landscape mapping [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **2026-03-05**: Formalized three-step deliverable approach and initiated landscape analysis data collection [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent observability, behavioral trace models, and session-level accountability standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding and technical conventions for AI agent observability and accountability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Operating as a coordination forum rather than a competing specification body, the working group aligns existing telemetry efforts (such as OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) and addresses interoperability gaps across agent frameworks and observability platforms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

The working group operates under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

# Scope and Technical Focus

The working group focuses on several core areas:
- **Session and Workflow Tracing**: Bridging the gap between single LLM call telemetry and session-level or multi-turn agent execution tracing across diverse tool calls and model interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Defining open trace models to prevent proprietary schema fragmentation and vendor lock-in[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Lineage and Accountability**: Establishing conventions for auditing, evaluating, and tracking content lineage across multi-modal agent workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Upstream Coordination**: Directing gap findings and proposed extensions upstream to existing standards bodies whenever possible[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Case Study Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines and requirements for AAIF member written and webinar case studies detailing open agentic standards adoption.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation Case Study Guidelines define criteria and submission formats for member organizations showcasing production implementations of open agentic AI standards, such as MCP, goose, and AGENTS.md[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]. The program provides reference implementations to the community while documenting tangible business impacts[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

# Participation and Formats

Member organizations can participate through two mechanisms[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]:
- **Written Case Studies**: Articles detailing customer or internal deployments, architectural approaches, and quantifiable outcomes.
- **Webinar Case Studies**: Recorded 20–30 minute presentations with Q&A hosted across AAIF publication channels.

Case studies are prioritized based on demonstrations of agentic maturity, open interoperability via protocol standards, and measurable operational acceleration[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem directory categorizing prominent open-source software and open standards in agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem directory mapping prominent open-source software projects, open standards, and AAIF member technologies across the agentic AI landscape[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. The landscape is generated using the CNCF Landscape2 engine and maintained through community contributions to its repository data files[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape representation is generated daily and incorporates project metadata and structured assets[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Generation Tooling**: Rendered using the `cncf/landscape2` generator platform[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Metadata and Data Enrichment**: Combines repository definitions in `landscape.yml` with metrics from GitHub and entity data from Crunchbase under data access licensing terms[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Update Cadence**: Processed daily, reflecting merged modifications within 24 hours[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Inclusion Guidelines
Entries submitted for inclusion must adhere to defined baseline criteria[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open Source Qualifications**: Open-source projects must have at least 1,000 GitHub stars and be assigned to a single best-fit category[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Exclusions**: Closed-source offerings, proprietary standards, commercial versions of open-source software, and closed-source products implementing open-source solutions are excluded[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Organization Placement**: Projects are typically limited to a single primary box per organization representing its principal offering[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Asset Standards**: Project logos must be in SVG format with English text, non-reversed backgrounds, and stacked orientations where variants exist[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Behavioral expectations, community standards, and enforcement scope governing participation across Agentic AI Foundation committees and activities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes standards for fostering an inclusive, welcoming, and safe environment across all Foundation activities[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Architecture / Specification
The Code of Conduct governs participation in AAIF Governing Board meetings, Technical Committee meetings ([`technical-committee`](../governance/technical-committee.md)), Working Group meetings, Outreach Committee meetings, and general Foundation activities not covered by separate project-specific policies[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

- **Foundation Events**: In-person and virtual events managed with professional event staff fall under the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct used in conjunction with this policy[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Technical Projects**: Umbrella technical projects operate as separate entities and maintain their own distinct codes of conduct for project participants[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

The policy defines expected behaviors—such as welcoming language, constructive collaboration, and respecting diverse viewpoints—alongside explicit prohibitions against discrimination, harassment, sustained disruption, personal attacks, and unauthorized distribution of private data[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Design principles, visual identity standards, and copy tone requirements ensuring neutral, collaborative, and trustworthy AAIF communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the core visual identity, typography, color palette, and copy tone required when creating or reviewing Agentic AI Foundation deliverables[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

# Architecture / Specification
The AAIF brand foundation rests on three pillars[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]:
- **Neutral**: Governance designed so no single vendor dominates the ecosystem. Materials prioritize balanced layouts, clear hierarchy, and open standards rather than winner-takes-all hype.
- **Collaborative**: Emphasizes shared ownership and cross-industry cooperation through inclusive, collective framing.
- **Trustworthy**: Builds on the Linux Foundation's neutral governance reputation by using clear, grounded claims, professional compositions, and strong typographic contrast.

Deliverables use a primary palette centered on white (`#ffffff`) and black (`#000000`) for high contrast, supported by secondary palettes and structured typographic scales[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

proposed_concept.description: Standardized repository of portable agent skills providing specialized domain instructions, references, and assets for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Public Agent Skills repository provides portable, modular capability packages containing instructions, references, scripts, and assets for autonomous AI agents[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification
Each agent skill is structured as an isolated directory adhering to the Agent Skills specification[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]:
- `SKILL.md`: Mandatory entrypoint containing YAML frontmatter metadata and structured Markdown execution instructions[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `assets/`: Static resources such as templates, logos, and imagery[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `references/`: Supporting documentation and extended technical specifications[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `scripts/`: Executable helper tooling[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

Skills are managed and installed via the Skills CLI (`npx skills`) and loaded contextually by compatible AI agent environments[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]. Published foundation skills include automated enforcement for the AAIF brand guidelines ([`brand-guidelines`](../policies/brand-guidelines.md))[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

proposed_concept.description: Standardized repository of portable agent resources providing reusable skills, recipes, prompt templates, and execution workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Public Agents initiative maintains an open collection of reusable agent assets, including domain skills, workflows, recipes, and prompt templates designed for portability across agentic platforms[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Architecture / Specification

The repository is structured into distinct asset categories[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]:
- `skills/`: Agent skills encapsulating domain expertise, workflows, and brand guidelines such as the AAIF Brand Guidelines skill[^evt-public-agents-pr-1].
- `recipes/`: Repeatable multi-step agent task workflows and operational routines.
- `prompts/`: Reusable prompts and structured prompt templates.
- `docs/`: Contribution guidelines and usage documentation.

## Workflow Automation and Testing

The initiative incorporates automated test workflows within `.github/workflows/` to validate model integrations and agent calls across backends:
- `copilot-test-action`: Queries the GitHub Models catalog and executes inference using repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` credentials[^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f].
- `gemini-test-action`: Validates prompt execution directly against the Google Gemini API using configured repository secrets[^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626].

# References

- [AAIF Public Agents Repository](https://github.com/aaif/public-agents)
- [Brand Guidelines Policy](../policies/brand-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) defines threat modeling standards, privacy guardrails, and architectural security patterns across agentic AI systems within the AAIF[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-WG Taxonomy Collaboration

Following working group chairs coordination, taxonomy harmonization was designated as the primary cross-working-group collaboration effort. The SP WG draft taxonomy serves as the foundational baseline to unify terminology across all AAIF working groups before divergent definitions emerge[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## External and Protocol Alignments

The working group tracks privacy and boundary implications of evolving agent protocols:
- **MCP Interceptors**: Reviewing proposed interception hooks in the Model Context Protocol for data redaction and security auditing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **MCP Apps**: Analyzing client-side and browser boundary security for embedded user interface extensions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-28**: Presented charter to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md); while procedural vote quorum fell short due to GitHub outages and non-votes, the group proceeded on consensus given absence of substantive objections. Operating cadence transitioned toward asynchronous deliverable workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# References

- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical oversight body of the Agentic AI Foundation, responsible for reviewing and approving working group charters, project proposals, and cross-cutting architectural standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing vendor-neutral standards for AI agent identity, attestation, delegation, and cross-organizational trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust (I&T) Working Group identifies and promotes vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its purpose is to enable agents to be discovered across platforms, prove their operating context, specify authorization chains, and execute auditable, privacy-preserving interactions across organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

The working group aligns with foundation governance under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and interfaces with the [Security & Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) and the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](./observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter covers six core areas of agent interaction[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Mechanisms for how agents identify themselves, authenticate, and communicate their software context and operational origin.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Protocols for representing actions taken on behalf of individuals, roles, teams, or services, including the limits of delegated authority.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns and policy constraints governing agent execution and human approval controls.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Verification and reasoning frameworks for assessing whether to trust external agents executing cross-boundary requests.
- **Agent Discovery and Metadata**: Interoperable metadata definitions supporting agent discovery, observability, and traceability.
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts**: Evaluation of deployment and identity patterns across diverse enterprise and consumer environments.

Explicitly out of scope are ratifying formal standards as a formal standards body, building production-grade identity hosting infrastructure, and defining general secure execution architectures covered by other groups[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter outlines initial goals including establishing operating structures, defining deliverable timelines, and coordinating cross-working group requirements within the AAIF[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Blog Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, submission intake workflows, and vendor-neutrality rules for publishing content on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) blog serves as a central platform for sharing updates, technical tutorials, and case studies across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Publishing on aaif.io is managed by the Linux Foundation team with community input submitted through a structured intake process [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

Contributors can automate and validate drafting against these guidelines using the `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill hosted in [Public Agents](../initiatives/public-agents.md) [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligible Contributors
- **Member Companies:** Permitted vendor-neutral posts, restricted to at most one or two closing sentences with a single external backlink [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Maintainers & Contributors:** Project updates and releases for hosted projects like MCP, goose, and AGENTS.md [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Working Groups & Technical Committee:** Official announcements and updates authored on behalf of working groups or the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Community Contributors:** Technical tutorials and community perspectives, capped at two submissions per month [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

## Content Standards
- **Neutrality:** Strictly non-promotional and vendor-neutral; content must not unduly favor one foundation member or criticize other open-source projects [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Originality & Timeliness:** Submissions must be original, previously unpublished, and cover events or work within the preceding two months [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Format:** Narrative structure, typically ranging between 600 and 1,500 words [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].
- **Lead Time:** Standard review and scheduling requires an approximate two-week lead time [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF coordination forum establishing agent observability conventions, session trace models, and standards alignment across the ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances agent observability by bringing together practitioners, vendors, and existing standards bodies to establish shared visibility into agent execution, evaluation, and safety [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Approved on May 13, 2026, the group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

The OT-WG is explicitly designed as a coordination forum rather than a duplicative standards organization, aiming to align existing specifications like OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context while upstreaming new work whenever possible [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Scope
- **Coordination Forum:** Identifies gaps across fragmented trace formats and proprietary platforms to prevent ecosystem vendor lock-in [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Workflow & Session Tracing:** Bridges the gap between single LLM call tracing and holistic, multi-turn, multi-modal agent session understanding [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Founding focus area developing vendor-neutral representations of agent actions, tool invocations, and state transitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

## Guiding Principles
1. Coordinate first, specify only when necessary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
2. Interoperability over innovation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
3. Observable by default [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
4. Vendor and framework neutrality [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security taxonomies, and containment design patterns for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Approved on May 13, 2026, and chaired by Alex Frazer, the group produces open threat models, taxonomies, and architectural design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

SPAA serves as a horizontal foundation layer across AAIF initiatives, helping peer groups such as [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md) and [Governance, Risk & Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) apply rigorous adversarial failure models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification

## In-Scope Activities
- **Threat Modeling & Attack Analysis:** Investigating prompt injection, confused deputy issues, authorization boundary breaches, and agent memory exploitation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Security Architecture & Design Patterns:** Formulating patterns for agent control, isolation, and blast-radius containment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Data Protection & Privacy:** Formulating mechanisms for handling autonomous data processing across multi-service boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Explicit Non-Goals
- **Ethics & Value Judgments:** Handled by governance bodies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Regulatory Interpretation:** Monitoring regulatory needs technically without prescribing compliance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **System Certification:** No direct vendor or tool certification programs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security taxonomies, design pattern catalogs, and containment practices for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (S&P WG) is an AAIF body tasked with defining pre-competitive security architectures, threat models, containment mechanisms, and safety practices across multi-agent environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] The group provides standardized guidance on mitigating risks unique to autonomous and tool-using systems, including prompt injection, multi-agent persuasion, unauthorized tool invocation, delegated authentication abuse, and cascading failure modes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope

The working group's scope covers foundational security disciplines for agentic AI:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Threat Modeling:** Identifying attack vectors across agent planning, tool selection, runtime memory, and inter-agent communication.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Containment and Control:** Defining patterns for human-in-the-loop (HITL) checkpoints, least-privilege tool execution, sandboxing, and execution hooks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Data Protection:** Establishing guardrails for agent memory persistence, context scrubbing, and personal data boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Cross-WG Security Reviews:** Formulating review criteria and checklists for other AAIF initiatives and working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

Explicitly out of scope are general AI ethics, regulatory compliance interpretations, and formal legal certifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]

## Deliverables and Workstreams

The working group organizes its technical output into dedicated workstreams and sequenced deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Near-term assessment analyzing gaps in existing threat modeling methodologies when applied to autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
2. **Security & Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Technical implementation catalog documenting design patterns (e.g., hooks, checkpoints, red teaming eval harnesses) and anti-patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
3. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide:** High-level operational and architectural guidance paired with the design patterns catalog.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
4. **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Early-stage checklist to facilitate cross-WG security evaluations across AAIF projects.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
5. **Taxonomy:** Originally drafted within S&P, foundational terminology work has been elevated to an AAIF-wide cross-working group initiative.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

## External Coordination

The group coordinates with adjacent standards initiatives and specifications, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem (MCP Apps, MCP ACS, interceptors, and hooks standardization) and external security standards such as AARM.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

# Governance and Operations

- **Leadership:** Led by Chair Alex Frazer and Co-Chair Junjie Bu.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Cadence:** Biweekly open all-hands meetings, with decentralized async coordination in workstream-specific channels.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Decision Making:** Operates by consensus with fallback to simple majority voting (51% quorum) and escalation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Licensing:** Code deliverables are released under Apache-2.0 or MIT; documentation is published under CC-BY-4.0 or CC-BY-SA 4.0 under the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape (AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map) is an interactive, CNCF Landscape 2-based directory categorizing open-source runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and regulatory regimes across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. It visualizes community projects alongside member technologies and tracks open-source momentum across the industry[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is built using the CNCF Landscape 2 framework and hosted via GitHub Pages and landscape2 tooling[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

### Project Tiers and Classification
The architecture map categorizes ecosystem entries into distinct tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]:
- **Graduated**: Mature projects meeting top-level governance, adoption, and security criteria.
- **Incubating**: Active projects demonstrating healthy adoption and ongoing development.
- **Member**: Projects and technologies maintained by AAIF member organizations.
- **External**: Ecosystem tools and third-party solutions operating in the broader landscape.

### Project Watchlist and LFX Insights Integration
The landscape decouples members and projects using distinct groupings and incorporates a dedicated watchlist for top agentic AI open-source projects, designed to sync with the Linux Foundation LFX Insights Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

### Validation and Preview Tooling
Continuous integration workflows automate schema validation and preview generation for pull requests:
- **Validation**: GitHub Actions leverage `cncf/landscape2-validate-action` to verify data (`landscape.yml`) and configuration (`settings.yml`) schemas on merge groups and pull requests[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].
- **Preview Generation**: Pull requests targeting `main` trigger automated comments providing dynamic visual overlay preview links on `aaif.landscape2.io`[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Client Protocol (ACP) Proposal
proposed_concept.description: Open protocol proposal standardizing communication between code editors/IDEs and AI coding agents to solve M×N integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) is an open protocol proposal submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to standardize communication between code editors or IDEs and AI coding agents[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]. Originating from Zed Industries and co-developed with JetBrains under the Apache 2.0 license, ACP aims to decouple agents from editor clients and resolve the M×N integration problem where each agent requires custom editor-specific integrations[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Architecture / Specification
ACP establishes a client-agent communication layer analogous to the Language Server Protocol (LSP) in software development tooling[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

### Protocol Scope and Transport
- **Editor-Agent UX Layer**: While the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes agent-to-tool and agent-to-data connectivity, ACP standardizes the editor-to-agent session interaction layer[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **MCP Complementarity**: ACP re-uses MCP JSON representations where appropriate and enables clients to configure MCP servers directly for their agents[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **Transports**: Supports JSON-RPC over `stdio` for local agent execution, with HTTP/WebSocket transport implementations in progress for remote agent workflows[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

### Governance and Specification Process
- **Maintainers**: Lead maintainers Ben Brandt (Zed Industries) and Sergey Ignatov (JetBrains), alongside core maintainers Agus Zubiaga, Anna Zhdan, and Niko Matsakis[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **RFD Process**: Uses a public Request for Dialog (RFD) process for changes to the specification[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Lifecycle History
- **Proposal Submitted**: Submitted to `aaif/project-proposals` with Technical Committee sponsorship discussion involving David Soria Parra[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy establishing the proposal requirements, stage criteria (Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review process for AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy governs how open technical projects join the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), progress across lifecycle stages, and undergo annual performance reviews.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] It defines structured expectations and support mechanisms across project maturity tiers to ensure vendor-neutral development and alignment with the Foundation's mission.

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Process
Projects join AAIF by submitting proposals to the technical committee and foundation repositories with specified metadata, including mission alignment, permissive OSI-approved licensing, governance documentation, release mechanics, and core maintainer lists.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] Proposing teams may also be paired with a mentor from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

## Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines three primary stages for foundation projects:[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30]
- **Growth Stage**: For projects demonstrating early adoption, active development, and clear alignment with foundation goals while building multi-organization contributor bases.
- **Impact Stage**: For mature, widely adopted projects that provide core infrastructure or standards for the agentic ecosystem and exhibit sustainable governance.
- **Emeritus Stage**: For projects reaching end-of-life or minimal activity, transitioning maintenance responsibility gracefully.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30]

## Annual Review Process
Projects undergo periodic evaluations to assess adoption, maintainer health, license compliance, and roadmap milestones, facilitating stage progression or retirement when appropriate.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]

proposed_concept.description: Editorial principles, platform tone baselines, and intake submission workflows for official Agentic AI Foundation social media channels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Social Media Governance and Guidelines document defines the operational strategy, editorial tone, and submission processes for official Agentic AI Foundation social channels operated under the Linux Foundation.[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637] The policy ensures that public foundation communication remains neutral, professional, inclusive, and strictly focused on open source AI ecosystem milestones and collaborative initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification

## Content Submission Channels
Community members and foundation participants can submit content for official social channels through two designated intake workflows:[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]
- **Direct Reposts**: Community-shared links and milestone announcements submitted via the dedicated Discord amplification channel.
- **Organic Foundation Posts**: Structured requests for foundation-authored posts submitted through the content intake form.

## Platform Standards and Etiquette
Official channels tailor their engagement style across platforms while maintaining vendor-neutrality:[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]
- **X**: Release announcements, short threads, and community highlights.
- **LinkedIn**: In-depth technical articles, case studies, and organizational achievements.
- **Bluesky**: Conversational community interaction, ideas, and open updates.

## Reposting and Moderation Rules
The Foundation restricts reposting to verified project releases, core contributor announcements, and standards implementations (such as MCP).[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637] Commercial advertisements, unsolicited vendor promotions, and personal blog posts without ecosystem-wide standard adoption are explicitly excluded. All interactions must adhere to the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines establish the framework for proposing, evaluating, and launching new Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] Working Groups serve as structured, time-bound collaborations where foundation members address critical technical, safety, policy, and governance challenges across the agentic AI domain.

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility and Submission Criteria
Submissions are restricted to member organizations in good standing across all Foundation membership tiers.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] Non-member submissions are not reviewed.

## Proposal Requirements
Working Group proposals must provide detailed charter information, including:[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a][^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4]
- **Submitter Information**: Lead contacts, organizational affiliations, and leadership availability.
- **Identity & Problem Statement**: Concise title, summary, specific challenge addressed, and alignment with AAIF strategic priorities.
- **Scope & Deliverables**: Concrete technical outputs such as whitepapers, benchmarks, specifications, or reference tooling.
- **Timeline & Structure**: Target operating cycle (typically 12–24 months) and proposed meeting cadence.
- **Membership & Expertise**: Necessary domain skill sets and confirmed participating organizations.
- **Impact, Urgency & Resources**: Clear rationale for foundation action, ecosystem benefit, and required infrastructure.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging and aligning open specifications, reference architectures, and interoperability patterns for AI agent-initiated commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) operates as a neutral forum to catalog, align, and harmonize open specifications, reference architectures, and interoperability models for commerce workflows conducted by AI agents[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the group focuses on converging emerging protocols across discovery, cart handoffs, payment execution, and post-purchase tracking while maintaining protocol neutrality rather than authoring competing commerce protocols[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
The Working Group explores interface specifications, risk signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and commerce ecosystems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- **Discovery & Negotiation:** Agent-merchant interfaces for real-time offers, inventory availability, commercial terms, and fulfillment options.
- **Cart & Checkout:** Data models for cart composition, validation, and execution handoffs between agent runtimes and merchant platforms.
- **Identity & Delegated Authority:** Buyer identity attestation and agent spending authority boundaries in coordination with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Agentic Payments:** Interfaces across agent wallets and payment networks (cards, real-time rails, and on-chain systems) for intent, authorization, and settlement signals.
- **Fraud Signaling & Autonomy Boundaries:** Risk-posture telemetry, human confirmation thresholds, and escalation pathways.
- **Post-Purchase Lifecycles:** Standardized interfaces for dispute initiation, chargeback signals, claims, and status updates.

Operational implementations of specific payment rails, fraud mitigation mechanisms, and proprietary marketplace systems remain explicitly out of scope[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was ratified on May 15, 2026, establishing ongoing reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes vendor-neutral security baselines, threat modeling frameworks, and architectural design patterns for autonomous and multi-agent AI environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. The working group operates under a formally approved charter to equip developers and governing bodies with tools to assess and mitigate risks unique to agent execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The group coordinates several focused deliverable tracks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Taxonomy and Landscape:** Surveying ecosystem tooling, frameworks, and shared nomenclature in cross-WG collaboration led by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** Analyzing threat vectors and establishing structured threat modeling methodologies for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Documenting defensive implementation patterns and architectural guardrails[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide:** Practical operational guidance for securing agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Shared review checklists used across the foundation to evaluate security and privacy readiness[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History
Following charter ratification in May 2026, workstreams transitioned to self-selected lead coordination models across active deliverable tracks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.description: Governance policy establishing proposal intake workflows, review criteria, stage transitions (Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and voting requirements for hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the stages, eligibility criteria, intake procedures, and review standards for open source projects hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. It establishes a transparent path for external and member-contributed software to progress through foundation-hosted stages under the technical supervision of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Submission Process
Prospective projects submit a standardized proposal issue within the `aaif/project-proposals` intake repository[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35]. Submitted applications follow structured lifecycle stages:
1. **Triage & Backlog:** Proposals receive initial triage and are scheduled for technical review.
2. **Review Presentation:** Project maintainers deliver a presentation to the Technical Committee with AAIF staff assistance[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Evaluation & Voting:** The Technical Committee reviews the application for alignment as either a Growth or Impact project. Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all Technical Committee members, followed by ratification from the Governing Board[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Proposal Status Labels
Applications are tracked on the public project board with explicit status states[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: Newly submitted application placed in the intake backlog.
- `Approved`: Accepted into the foundation hosting structure.
- `Declined`: Application declined with documented feedback.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Review pending maintainer clarifications.
- `Too Early`: Project not yet mature enough for stage requirements.

## Reapplication and Membership Conditions
- **Reapplication Window:** Declined projects may reapply after addressing reviewer feedback, with a mandatory 3-month cooldown period showing tangible progress[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Membership Neutrality:** Submitting or hosting a project does not require AAIF corporate membership, nor does project hosting confer governing board representation or corporate membership tier status[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) serves as a bridge between global AI policy developments and technical advancements in agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. It addresses the lack of cohesive regulatory guidance, standards, and risk mitigation strategies across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group analyzes governance models, deployment policies, and technical standards needed to ensure safe adoption of open agentic systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

## In Scope
- Tracking and analyzing emerging global regulations, standards, and policy frameworks affecting agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Evaluating organizational-level governance implementation for agent protocols (e.g., Model Context Protocol) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Action reversibility characterization and undo infrastructure protocols for reversible agent actions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- AI Agent Bill of Materials (AABOM) standards covering models, scaffolding, tools, APIs, and component provenance [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Risk assessment classifications, incident reporting policies, and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) autonomy definitions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Evaluating and adopting domain-specific frameworks such as the FINOS AI Governance Framework [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

## Out of Scope
- Providing formal legal advice or compliance certification solutions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Endorsing specific commercial tools or proprietary vendor solutions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Governance and Leadership
The working group is led by Primary Contact Ryan Hagemann (IBM) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. Charters and core deliverables are submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for formal review and ratification [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the proposal intake, review, and approval process for forming new working groups under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Architecture / Specification
Proposals are created through issue templates in the working group proposals repository and tracked publicly across proposal lifecycle stages [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Application and Review Process
1. **Submission**: Applicants open a structured issue proposal and provide charter goals, scope, and leadership contacts [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
2. **Triage & Review**: Proposals enter the backlog and are scheduled for evaluation during formal [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) meetings [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
3. **Voting**: To be accepted, a proposal must receive a simple majority vote from the Technical Committee, subject to final approval by the Governing Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Status Labels
Proposals are categorized by standardized status labels [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: The proposal is newly submitted and queued in the backlog for triage [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Approved`: The proposal has received required approvals [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Declined`: The proposal was declined with documented feedback provided in comments [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Additional clarification or revisions are required from submitters [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Too Early`: The proposal is premature, with guidance provided for future reapplication [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral conventions, telemetry standards, and tracing protocols for agentic AI architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives through dedicated focus groups and asynchronous GitHub workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

## Focus Groups
- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Develops telemetry standards and distributed trace propagation models for multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Observability and Protocols**: Evaluates protocol-level telemetry integration and standardization across agent communication layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group focuses on developing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, privacy-preserving architectures, and security review baselines across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing authority of the Agentic AI Foundation. It oversees project lifecycle transitions, reviews working group progress, aligns architecture across initiatives, and arbitrates cross-project technical dependencies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa, ^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Architecture / Specification
## Monthly Working Group Reporting
Working groups and workstreams maintain visibility with the Technical Committee through standardized monthly markdown reports submitted via GitHub pull requests [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32]:
- **Intake Timeline**: Reports are submitted by working group chairs by the last business day of each reporting month [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee conducts an asynchronous review that closes 7 calendar days after submission [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- **Standard Structure**: Reports summarize monthly progress against objectives, highlight blockers and risks, detail next-month priorities, and explicitly surface required Technical Committee decisions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, working groups across the foundation adopted the asynchronous monthly reporting pull request template to maintain non-blocking visibility with the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa, ^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing threat models, design pattern catalogs, and cross-group security review checklists for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops shared threat models, security taxonomies, design pattern catalogs, and cross-functional security guidance across the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. The working group functions as an intersecting review layer across AAIF initiatives, assessing security boundaries, privacy safeguards, and threat exposure in sister working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams

### Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
Evaluates existing AI threat modeling frameworks (such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic-AI-specific threats including multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation hazards, delegated authorization boundaries, and prompt/tool supply-chain integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Leads**: Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]

### Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
Curates reusable patterns and anti-patterns for agent security, including execution hooks, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, privacy-preserving runtime execution (TEE, zero-knowledge, encrypted vector storage), blast radius containment, memory lifecycle controls, kill switches, and authorization boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Leads**: Dan Kommatas (Circle), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]

### Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist
Maintains operational checklists and intake mechanisms to evaluate deliverables produced by other AAIF groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Key initial targets include:
- [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Agent identity attestation and delegated authorization models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Payments guardrails, fund drain prevention, and agent scope limits[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- **Lead**: Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

### Taxonomy and Terms Coordination
The working group's initial terms and definitions deliverable transitioned into the cross-WG Taxonomy / Landscape workstream (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) to form unified AAIF-wide terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **WG Delegates**: Jay White (Microsoft), Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]

# Lifecycle History
Deliverables follow a structured progression defined in repository guidelines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:
- **Draft**: Work in progress prefixed with `DRAFT-`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Formally approved by a recorded working group meeting decision in meeting notes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: Transferred to cross-working-group workstreams or dedicated repositories, retaining redirect notes and inbound links[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing threat models, design pattern catalogs, best practice guides, and cross-group security reviews for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group focuses on identifying security and privacy challenges in agentic AI systems, defining threat models, publishing mitigation best practices, and conducting security reviews across Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group collaborates with external standards organizations such as OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, Cloud Security Alliance (CSA), and NIST[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical activities across five primary workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

1. **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates gaps in existing AI threat frameworks (such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) relative to agentic-specific threats, including memory poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, excessive agency, and delegated authorization boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
2. **Design Patterns Catalog**: Catalogs reusable security and privacy patterns using a problem, context, solution, and trade-off format[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
3. **Best Practices Guide**: Provides higher-level practical guidance and external framework pointers covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
4. **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Develops lightweight security and privacy review processes and checklists for artifacts produced by other AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
5. **Taxonomy**: Originating in this working group, vocabulary efforts were elevated to the foundation-wide cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream led by Junjie Bu, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as delegates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy draft transitioned to a foundation-wide initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Repositories made public; monthly update cadence to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) formalized; workstream directory structure and GitHub-first documentation practices confirmed[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Foundation-wide AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology, failure taxonomy, and landscape classification across working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a foundation-wide AAIF initiative tasked with building unified terminology, defining agent archetypes, and resolving conflicting definitions across all working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Originating from early work in the [Security and Privacy WG](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the initiative now maintains an independent repository to coordinate vocabulary across domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates as a cross-cutting coordination body led by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Each working group designates delegates to contribute 10–20 core domain terms, review shared concepts, and resolve duplicate definitions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

Taxonomy topics and schema slices under active integration across working groups include[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4]:
- System boundaries and evaluation subjects
- Accuracy, output quality, and reliability dimensions
- Operational, governance, and grounding terms
- Failure vocabularies (symptoms and root causes)
- Metrics, measurement, and evaluation ecosystems
- Agent capability archetypes (e.g., tool invocation, network access limits)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Escalated from Security & Privacy WG into a cross-WG initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed as lead[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Working groups appoint official delegates (e.g., Jay White and Katherine Druckman for Security & Privacy)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates runtime context representation, persistent memory states, and product/academic landscape patterns[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, and architectural practices for agent accuracy, reliability, and failure recovery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to establish the standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for autonomous AI agents to operate accurately and reliably in real-world enterprise environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group addresses non-determinism in agentic workloads by classifying failure modes, defining measurement and detection frameworks, and standardizing recovery patterns[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification
## Principles and Technical Scope
ARWG operates under four guiding principles: reliability and accuracy by design, empirical grounding of recommendations, vendor neutrality, and transparency as a prerequisite[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

Technical focus areas in scope include[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation dimensions, metrics, failure mode taxonomies, and performance thresholds for autonomous systems.
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Establishing proactive structural requirements, including verification loops and grounding mechanisms against authoritative systems of record and trust anchors.
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Formulating specifications for safe-state restoration, automated rollback, compensatory actions, and handoff triggers for human-in-the-loop intervention.

Explicitly out of scope are foundation model training, prompt engineering, commercial guardrail tooling, domain-specific legal compliance, and trace emission mechanics (which are delegated to the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md))[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group organizes its output into canonical deliverables D1 through D6 and internal workstream items[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]:
- **D1 (Accuracy & Reliability Taxonomy & Vocabulary)**: Architectural framing covering evaluation subjects, output quality, root causes, failure symptoms, and correction mechanisms, harmonized in liaison with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey)**: Applied field analysis assessing operational requirements across enterprise personas (PMs, ops, evaluators, data scientists) to drive the D6 evaluation protocol scope[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-29**: June 2026 progress report filed, establishing biweekly plenary and deliverable sessions, cross-WG liaisons with Observability and Taxonomy groups, and advancing D1 taxonomy and D2 gap analysis tracks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

proposed_concept.description: Foundation-wide AAIF workstream establishing shared agentic AI taxonomy schemas, terminology harmonization across working groups, and interactive ecosystem landscape mapping.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative charged with constructing a shared terminology standard and an interactive ecosystem landscape directory to prevent siloed research and terminology collisions across foundation working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] The workstream serves as a cross-cutting harmonization body comprised of active delegates and domain editors nominated from across AAIF working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

# Architecture / Specification

## Taxonomy and Landscape Data Models

The workstream operates on a decoupled architecture separating data definitions from presentation layers:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Taxonomy Metadata Schema**: Implements a SKOS Lite data model structuring concepts with both concise summaries and detailed scope notes to support varying technical depths.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Landscape Mapping Schema**: Adopts the CNCF-style landscape tool metadata format to catalog open-source agentic frameworks, runtime components, and external industry entities, integrated alongside [Agentic AI Landscape](agentic-ai-landscape.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]
- **Standards Alignment**: Taxonomy definitions prioritize alignment with established international frameworks from standards bodies such as ISO and NIST, documenting explicit rationale where domain deviations are necessary.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]

## Contribution and Review Workflow

Contributions follow an asynchronous, PR-driven workflow:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
1. **Term Intake and Aggregation**: Initial candidate terms and cross-working-group concepts are consolidated into shared review sheets and pull requests to identify overlaps and boundary edge cases.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
2. **Domain Editor Review**: Working group delegates and designated domain editors review overlapping terms, resolve boundary ambiguities, and enforce editorial style guidelines requiring human curation oversight.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
3. **TC Reporting**: The workstream submits monthly progress reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the last business day of each month, subject to a 7-day review window.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Workstream convened to align on charter scope, decoupled repository structure, and SKOS Lite metadata modeling.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
- **2026-06-01**: Formally adopted CNCF landscape metadata schemas and asynchronous PR review workflows.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **2026-06-08**: Formed delegate core group and converted legacy terms into structured PRs.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]
- **2026-06-15**: Established standard alignment policies (ISO/NIST) and human curation requirements for taxonomy definitions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]
- **2026-06-22**: Finalized delegate rosters across working groups and initiated cross-group agent boundary definitions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate June 2026 milestone achievements including SKOS-Lite schema definitions, delegates onboarding, and July 2026 terminology review workflow.

proposed_concept.description: Foundation-wide AAIF workstream establishing SKOS-Lite agentic AI taxonomy schemas, terminology harmonization, and CNCF-style ecosystem landscapes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a foundation-wide initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with developing standardized terminology, machine-readable conceptual schemas, and ecosystem mapping for agentic AI systems[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream brings together appointed delegates from participating working groups across the foundation to unify domain vocabulary and catalog open-source components[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates through two primary technical artifacts and publishing pipelines:
- **Taxonomy Schema**: Employs a SKOS-Lite data schema to model agentic concepts, relationships, and universal versus domain-specific terminology[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Implements a CNCF-style interactive landscape configuration format to categorize agentic software, protocols, and tooling[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Web Portal and CI/CD**: An automated publishing pipeline and development environment hosts the public taxonomy and landscape portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

## Terminology Harmonization Process
The workstream coordinates terminology intake from all AAIF working groups, including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Governance, Risk and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Working groups contribute batches of core terms that are aggregated into a unified review document to resolve semantic collisions before creating formal pull requests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Terms undergo peer review with classifications including universal terms, debate candidates, and consensus-based culling of non-agent-specific terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Finalized and approved workstream charter across participating working groups; defined SKOS-Lite and CNCF-style schemas; onboarded working group delegates and ingested initial batches of domain terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **July 2026**: Advanced unified terminology review across ~250 candidate terms, establishing structured consensus tagging, cull workflows, and universal term prioritization[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

mutations.rationale: Update with June 2026 reporting deliverables, focus group structure, and July 2026 focus group consolidation and trace model explorations.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open standards, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for monitoring, tracing, and debugging AI agent operations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group addresses unique challenges in agentic execution such as non-deterministic reasoning steps, tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, and context propagation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical scope through specialized focus areas and alignment with related foundation efforts:

## Focus Groups
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Addressing instrumentation baselines for language model operations and inter-agent communication protocols (consolidated from separate primitive and protocol streams)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Standardizing telemetry for multi-agent coordination, handoffs, and workflow orchestration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic State, Context & Reasoning**: Defining representations for tracing dynamic state mutations, prompt contexts, and reasoning trajectories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

## Inter-Group & Initiative Collaborations
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Contributes domain-specific observability definitions to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic Trace Models & Discovery**: Developing trace model architectures and evaluating integration with emerging specifications such as Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Initiated charter deliverables, launched five initial focus groups, and submitted baseline use case and gap analysis documents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **July 2026**: Initiated focus group consolidation to streamline deliverables, began evaluation of trace models, and reviewed external resource discovery integration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
