proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group (also designated Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) aligns agentic AI technical standards with international policy frameworks, regulatory mandates, and risk management practices[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group evaluates governance mechanisms to ensure compliant and accountable agent deployments across regulated industries[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group produces policy mappings, regulatory alignment matrices, and gap analysis artifacts:
- **Policy Landscape Mapping**: Cataloging existing international policy frameworks, government guidance documents, and industry risk standards applicable to agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Comparative & Gap Analysis**: Assessing current technical safeguards against regulatory baselines to identify standards and tooling gaps[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Cross-Workstream Alignment**: Contributing regulatory and governance terminology into the foundation's shared vocabulary through the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Completed the initial 3-month landscape mapping of existing agentic AI policy frameworks and guidance standards[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **July 2026**: Initiated a 3-month sprint focusing on comparative gap analysis against regulatory baselines[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, architectural design patterns, security best practice guides, and review checklists for agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group coordinates across five active workstreams and interfaces with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and cross-foundation initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical program around five primary workstreams and deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating frameworks including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF to identify agentic security gaps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security guidelines and risk mitigations for agent developers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining standard architectural patterns for secure agent integration[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing intake evaluation criteria and security checklists across AAIF technical deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman supporting the cross-foundation [Taxonomy and Landscape](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Operational Workflows
The working group submits monthly progress reports to the Technical Committee by the last business day of each month, followed by a seven-day async review window before report merging[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]. The group also seeks collaboration with external industry efforts such as OWASP, AARM, and FINOS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-30**: Submitted and merged the June 2026 monthly report marking transition from formation to execution across five workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].
- **2026-07-07**: Reviewed threat modeling gap analysis deliverable, first draft of best practices guide, and MCP tool attestation security patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Initiative is a foundation-wide workstream led by Junjie Bu that standardizes terminology, definitions, and ecosystem classifications across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. It harmonizes domain-specific terms across all working groups into a unified taxonomy and coordinates with the [Agentic AI Landscape](../initiatives/agentic-ai-landscape.md) ecosystem directory[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The initiative operates a pull request-driven, schema-based terminology curation model using CNCF-style landscape definitions and SKOS-Lite structures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. Key operational elements include:
- **Cross-WG Representation**: Each AAIF working group designates core delegates (for instance, Jay White and Katherine Druckman from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) to contribute and review domain terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Unified Term Curation**: Terms are collected in a centralized review sheet where contributors track attribution and consensus before converting entries into repository pull requests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Disambiguation and Standards**: The workstream resolves high-level boundary definitions, such as differentiating autonomous AI agents from broader bots, and distinguishing conceptual terms such as Agent Card versus Agent Blueprint[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting established charter review and PR-driven taxonomy workflow[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-06-01 to 2026-06-22**: Formed core delegate team across working groups and transitioned taxonomy from individual WG scope into a foundation-wide initiative[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **2026-07-06**: Transitioned into the active execution phase reviewing the unified taxonomy sheet and established weekly one-hour syncs[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is an official Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) cross-working group body established to eliminate terminology fragmentation and avoid redundant ecosystem analysis across technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Rather than dictating vertical domain specifications, the workstream unifies domain glossaries into a reconciled SKOS-Lite taxonomy and maintains an authoritative, interactive ecosystem map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Curation Model and Guardrails
The workstream operates on a horizontal curation model while preserving vertical ownership within specific technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]:
- **Consolidation over Creation:** The workstream ingests and harmonizes glossaries provided by technical working groups rather than creating domain terms in isolation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **SKOS-Lite Schema:** Vocabulary concepts are structured with fields including `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Portal Automation:** An automated GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline packages the taxonomy explorer and CNCF Landscape 2 datasets, rendering and deploying static distribution artifacts to GitHub Pages[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

# Governance and Operations
- **Approval Date:** 2026-06-21[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Chairs:** Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg, Co-Chair)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Delegate Representation:** Each working group nominates two Domain Editor delegates to resolve terminology overlaps during weekly synchronization sessions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. The working group provides interoperability guidance and reference architectures spanning discovery, negotiation, checkout, payment orchestration, and post-purchase interactions while maintaining strict protocol neutrality[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

Rather than authoring competing commerce protocols, the group identifies common ground across existing and emerging specifications and presents strategic paths forward to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope and Focus Areas
- **Discovery & Negotiation:** Standardizing agent-to-catalog discovery and autonomous negotiation patterns[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Checkout & Payment Orchestration:** Coordinating cross-framework transaction execution, delegation, and payment flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Post-Purchase Lifecycle:** Harmonizing multi-system post-purchase interactions, fulfillment tracking, and dispute management[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

### Leadership and Governance
- **Chair:** Ilya Grigorik (Shopify)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Co-Chair:** Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Appointed Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 (appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, extending open specifications to produce interoperability guidelines and design patterns across execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Approved by governance on May 13, 2026, the group addresses portability barriers, long-running stateful execution, external tool coordination, and failure recovery across agent frameworks[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification

### Technical Scope
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Standardizing primitives (tasks, tool calls, branching, retries, sub-agents) and execution semantics (step ordering, parallelism, conditional branching, agent handoffs)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Defining execution patterns for workflows spanning minutes to days, handling partial completion, workflow state persistence, idempotency, failure recovery, and workflow-level audit history (distinguished from runtime traces managed by [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md))[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Tool Invocation & External Coordination:** Formulating patterns for interacting with external APIs, CLIs, external enterprise services, and human-in-the-loop reviewers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

### Leadership
- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes vendor-neutral security frameworks, threat models, design pattern catalogs, and best practice guides for agentic AI architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]. The group evaluates emerging agent attack surfaces—such as prompt injection, tool-use hijacking, and MCP poisoning—by modeling decomposed agent archetypes (I/O channels, models, conversation histories, tool orchestration, prompts, and resources)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

# Architecture / Specification

### Deliverables and Workstreams
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing baseline threat models and gap analyses[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing implementation baselines grounded in foundational industry literature and community inputs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, categorizing reusable architectural mitigations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing cross-group review checklists and reviewing scopes across [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Alignment:** Contributing security and privacy terminology (such as session replay constraints, guardrails, and agent definitions) to the cross-group [Taxonomy & Landscape](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort led by Junjie Bu, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as working group delegates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) develops vendor-neutral standards, benchmarks, terminology frameworks, and architectural guidance to evaluate and improve the accuracy, consistency, robustness, and operational reliability of autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and taxonomy for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, action records, and trust verification.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] The working group is chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical work across three specialized sub-working groups:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Taxonomy Sub-WG:** Defines core primitives including Agent, Action Record, Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop boundaries. The group establishes the Action Record as a tamper-evident, content-private, verifiable record of a consequential action intended for counterparties and auditors, distinct from operational telemetry developed in [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Reference Architecture Sub-WG:** Maintains a component architecture matrix spanning Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation. Architectural baselines enforce monotonic authorization containment where delegated sub-agents cannot hold broader permissions than their delegating agents or initiating human users.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Critical Use Cases Sub-WG:** Develops operational lifecycle requirements across Internal, B2B, and B2C environments covering naming, deployment, delegation, access control, audit, and revocation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

The working group profiles OAuth 2.0 as the normative cross-platform presentation baseline for agent tokens, delegation chains, and scope expressions while leaving backend policy evaluation autonomous.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] Technical inputs evaluated include NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) reference design and OpenID Foundation identity management frameworks.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Lifecycle History
The working group was formed under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to address open agent identity, attestation, and delegation standards.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] In mid-2026, the working group established sub-WG tracks and advanced baseline authorization proposals to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group developing open specifications, capability maps, and interoperability guidance for autonomous commercial interactions and shopping agents.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393] The group is co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains a protocol-neutral focus on commerce-facing interfaces across the transaction lifecycle:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map:** The core foundational deliverable categorizing functional interfaces across product discovery, delegated authority, negotiation, checkout, payment, fraud signaling, and post-purchase handling.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Discovery & Catalog Feeds:** Distinguishes asynchronous catalog feeds from dynamic merchant and marketplace retrieval, addressing product normalization, source freshness, and trust boundaries.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Negotiation & Checkout:** Evaluates stateful merchant-authoritative checkout negotiations, transport bindings, extension models, and human-handoff patterns across protocols like ACP and UCP.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Payment Handler Model:** Structures payment operations around three reusable abstractions: handler, instrument, and credential, evaluating composition models with the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Trust & Fraud Signaling:** Coordinates with [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to isolate shopper identity and risk from agent platform identity and transaction delegation evidence.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

# Lifecycle History
The working group drafted its foundational charter in April 2026 to scope interface boundaries separate from backend merchant system internals.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760] The charter was approved by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in May 2026, transitioning the working group into comparative protocol analyses and Capability Map development.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group mapping open commerce protocols, capability models, fraud/trust signals, and wallet handoffs across the transaction lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation body focused on aligning open specifications, establishing capability maps, and providing neutral interoperability guidance across the agentic commerce lifecycle [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses fragmentation across platforms, agents, merchants, payment networks, and risk systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].

Rather than introducing a competing proprietary protocol, the working group develops neutral landscape evaluations and reference frameworks that synthesize existing protocol inputs, including Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agent Client Protocol (ACP), Agent Payment Protocol (AP2), and x402 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

# Architecture / Specification

## Commerce Lifecycle Framework

The working group structures its landscape and capability mapping around a four-phase user journey [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

1. **Discovery:** Comparing feed-based and live-query models for source discovery, catalog normalization, freshness, and merchant trust [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation:** Evaluating transport bindings, dynamic negotiations, presentation schemas, and human handoff mechanisms [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
3. **Payment and Wallets:** Analyzing credential provision, x402 payment responses, and AP2 bounded intent mandates within multi-turn agent interactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
4. **Post-Purchase:** Distinguishing passive order status observation from state-changing mutations such as returns, refunds, cancellations, and dispute arbitration [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

## Cross-Cutting Concerns and Signal Exchange

The working group investigates how trust and fraud signals flow when context is distributed across agents, merchants, payment providers, and risk engines [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]. Core focus areas include separating agent identity from shopper identity, establishing evidence binding delegated authority to transactions, and supporting risk-triggered or baseline evidence exchanges while minimizing unnecessary data exposure [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

These cross-cutting requirements align with work in related foundation bodies, including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026:** Kickoff survey identified core actor roles, cross-cutting requirements, and protocol fragmentation risks [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026:** Formulated the four-stage commerce lifecycle methodology and problem-first gap analysis model [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **June 2026:** Analyzed fraud, trust signals, and signal provenance across distributed multi-actor transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **July 2026:** Advanced post-purchase mutation analysis and evaluated agent wallet integration patterns [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with establishing a unified agentic AI terminology and maintaining the ecosystem landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates terminology across foundation working groups and operates the public Taxonomy and Landscape Portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

The workstream coordinates across domain-specific groups to eliminate conflicting terminology and maintain alignment with the [Agentic AI Landscape](./agentic-ai-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification

## Terminology Review Methodology

The workstream operates on a sequenced review model to manage a foundation-wide terminology backlog [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:

- **Admission Before Definition:** Terms are first evaluated and admitted or culled as recognized concept entries before definitions, categories, and broader term relationships are locked [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Arbitration Pipeline:** Terms originating from universal domains or specific working groups (such as [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)) undergo group review to resolve contested meanings [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Public Portal:** Agreed terms are published via version-controlled pull requests directly to the open Taxonomy and Landscape Portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026:** Transitioned from backlog collection to systematic term arbitration; admitted the first batch of 13 terms via PR #33, launching the initial live public taxonomy portal entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **August 2026:** Cumulative reviews reached 67 out of 128 backlog terms, with 21 admitted to the taxonomy, 15 culled, and 25 contested terms held for structured cross-group debate [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

mutations.rationale: Captures the Human Approval Gate workflow pattern established by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern ensuring an authorized human explicitly reviews and decides on an immutable proposal before protected actions execute.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate is a workflow pattern designed to ensure that when a workflow reaches an action with high risk, audit obligations, or ownership constraints, an accountable and uniquely identified human must decide whether the exact proposal may cause a protected effect[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. The workflow remains safely parked in a durable wait state and cannot execute the protected action until explicit approval is granted[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

# Architecture / Specification
In this pattern, an immutable proposal is presented to an authorized human principal via an interaction surface while the workflow execution engine halts execution awaiting a decision[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

Key invariants include:
- The approver must be a uniquely identified human principal authorized for the decision class; shared approval accounts do not qualify[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- The interface displays the exact, immutable proposal version to which the decision binds[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- Approval and rejection must be explicit decisions; timeouts, delivery failures, or system silence never constitute implicit approval[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- The decision record captures proposal version, approver identity, decision outcome, and timestamp within the run's audit trail[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- Changed or superseded proposals invalidate previous pending approvals and require re-approval[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- Pending approval states must enforce explicit deadlines and escalation paths, preventing duplicate or conflicting decision executions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

Required capabilities include an execution engine, a human interaction surface, a state/context store, and an audit log[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

# Lifecycle History
Defined within the reference architectures workstream in `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural decision proposal organizing AAIF reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural agent counts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model is an architectural decision proposed within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`) to organize reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural topology such as single-agent or multi-agent categories[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Architecture / Specification
Under this decision framework:
- A **Reference Architecture** is defined as a complete composition of reusable patterns, required capabilities, boundaries, guarantees, and exit states tailored to a recognizable practitioner job[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- A **Pattern** is an independently adoptable solution to a single recurring workflow problem (retaining its own invariants, failure modes, and implementation examples)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- Single-agent and multi-agent topologies are treated as structural characteristics used within architectures rather than top-level categorization criteria[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- Practical use cases and scenarios validate architectures to identify missing variants or distinct jobs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed on 2026-07-20 for working group review within `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing telemetry standards, distributed trace models, and session observability frameworks for agentic AI architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open telemetry standards, distributed tracing primitives, and runtime observability frameworks across single- and multi-agent systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]. The group addresses challenges in capturing non-deterministic decision paths, tool invocation sequences, cross-boundary agent communication, and verifiable execution trails[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification

## Focus Tracks

To improve participation and streamline cross-cutting efforts, the working group consolidated into three active tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:

- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, this track focuses on Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) observability (tracing skill discovery, provenance, governance, and pre-execution trust decisions), treating skills as first-class citizens in telemetry models, and developing cross-boundary gap models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination)**: Led by Ty Smith, exploring modular observability maps and context intelligence runtime tracking across multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Agentic State & Context**: Led by Govindaraj, combining reasoning and state observability into unified gap and landscape analyses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

## Active Initiatives

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A proposal standardizing application-layer trace models and bridging OpenTelemetry (OTEL) core specifications with agentic lifecycle requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Verifiable Telemetry and Peer-to-Peer Observability**: Collaborations involving Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) encoded via CBOR to enable verifiable, transport-agnostic telemetry across peer-to-peer agent networks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Close coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define universal observability terms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Lifecycle History

- Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- In July 2026, the working group restructured its operational focus groups from five to three tracks to reduce overlap and accelerate deliverable execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow models, common primitives, and operational integration standards across agentic execution frameworks.

# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing shared workflow models, open interoperability guidelines, and design patterns that allow agent workflows to operate seamlessly across diverse frameworks, tools, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstreams

- **Taxonomy**: Establishes a standardized vocabulary and core workflow definitions to eliminate ambiguity across specifications and architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Reference Architectures**: Develops architecture blueprints and integration patterns applying common workflow primitives[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Catalogs representative end-to-end operational use cases evaluating agent execution across enterprise process boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a working group deliverable establishing operational controls and mitigation patterns across agentic system design and deployment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide provides failure-pattern analyses, security controls, and decision frameworks for engineers building agentic workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide defines operational security recommendations across five primary domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
- **Secrets Management**: Strategies and controls for managing, scoping, and protecting sensitive credentials and API keys used by autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Tool execution security, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and supply chain controls protecting against malicious or compromised capabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Guardrails**: Input and output filtering mechanisms, semantic boundary enforcement, and runtime policy validation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Automated and manual testing methodologies to benchmark and evaluate agent security postures before and during production[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Diagnostic practices, telemetry artifact retention, and forensic analysis procedures following security events[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

### Scope Boundaries
Delegated authorization architectures and cryptographic agent identity standards (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are explicitly excluded from this guide and are maintained by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History
- **Draft v0.1**: Initial draft deliverable submitted under PR #9 covering core security domains, failure patterns, and tool maturity reference matrices[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group responsible for developing threat models, architecture design pattern catalogs, operational security guidelines, and controls for agentic artificial intelligence systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables across five active workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]:
- **Threat Modeling & Gap Analysis**: Documenting agent-specific attack vectors, vulnerabilities, and failure modes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: Practitioner-oriented controls spanning secrets management, secure tool invocation (MCP), guardrails, eval frameworks, and forensics in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural and operational design patterns for secure agent execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Security and privacy vocabulary alignment coordinated with the foundation-wide [Taxonomy and Landscape Initiative](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **Identity & Authorization Coordination**: Cross-WG boundary ensuring identity and attestation standards (e.g. SPIFFE/SVID, RFC 8693) are driven by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Formed five active workstreams with leads and transitioned taxonomy alignment to the cross-WG effort[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **July 2026**: Published first open draft pull requests for Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and the Best Practices Guide, and finalized the Design Patterns Catalog structure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group develops open threat models, security and privacy design patterns, cross-group review checklists, and best practice guides enabling providers, consumers, and peer working groups to maintain shared responsibility for secure agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operations

- **Chairs:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. Meetings and repositories default to open public access[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Review & Merge Process:** Workstream deliverables within the approved charter can be reviewed and merged directly by the working group on GitHub without requiring prior [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval, with progress reported asynchronously via monthly reports[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].

## Core Workstreams and Deliverables

1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Analyzes threat modeling gaps against frameworks such as MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, evaluating STRIDE and PASTA alignments for agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** A comprehensive guide covering threat mitigation, human-in-the-loop controls, and failure recovery, coordinating with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) for identity and authorization coverage[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. See [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md).
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** A structured catalog of reusable architectural security patterns and templates for agentic deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** A collaborative checklist and gap analysis model ensuring security consistency across AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration:** Contributing security- and privacy-specific terms into the foundation-wide taxonomy initiative in collaboration with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17:** Orientation meeting and initial problem area ideation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-03-03:** Alex Frazer introduced as chair[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-04-14:** Charter and five initial deliverables approved unanimously by working group vote[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-05-26:** Charter officially approved by the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-07-31:** Initial draft pull requests submitted for the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **2026-08-04:** Working group resolved to default all meeting recordings and resources to open access and confirmed autonomous repository merge workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

Produced under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide outlines controls across model execution, tool integration, human oversight, and data boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstream Scope and Ownership

- **Cross-WG Collaboration:** Identity, authentication, and authorization sections are coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to maintain distinct architectural boundaries and avoid duplicated specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Hardware-isolated policy enforcement and evidence signing pattern gating agent data release on independent verifier appraisal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime is a design pattern developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for agentic AI deployments where the infrastructure operator is considered part of the threat model[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. It isolates the Policy Decision Point (PDP) and evidence signer inside a hardware-isolated environment (such as a Trusted Execution Environment or TEE) while keeping agent workload execution outside the boundary to avoid enlarging the Trusted Computing Base (TCB)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern defines four mandatory elements necessary to maintain policy integrity and verifiable execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
1. **Isolated Enforcement Point**: Isolate policy evaluation and decision logic within a hardware boundary while keeping agent code outside, mitigating the risk of untrusted prompt inputs compromising the TCB[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Generate cryptographic evidence-signing keys inside the hardware boundary and bind all generated execution evidence to those keys[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
3. **Measurement-Sealed Policy**: Cryptographically seal the active policy bundle to the runtime's measured state, releasing decryption capabilities only after successful attestation appraisal[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
4. **Per-Unit-of-Work Appraisal**: Gate data release and execution steps on verification of per-unit-of-work evidence by an independent appraisal service[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

The specification supports multiple hardware mechanisms—including AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0—and aligns with RFC 9334 (RATS Architecture), RFC 9711 (COSE), RFC 8747, IETF SCITT, and SLSA[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. It also specifies a software-only operational mode for testing and development in environments without confidential computing hardware[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08 (PR #11)**: Introduced as an initial draft pattern in the `wg-security-and-privacy` design-patterns workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem map modeled on the CNCF Landscape that categorizes open-source and standard technologies across the agentic AI infrastructure stack[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape organizes projects across key categories including:
- **Frameworks & Infrastructure**: Encompasses orchestration engines, multi-agent frameworks, and AI gateways. Key subcategories include **Orchestration & Multi-Agent**, which tracks multi-protocol AI gateways such as Higress and Solo.io's agentgateway that provide unified control planes for Model Context Protocol (MCP) server hosting, agent-to-agent communication, and LLM inference governance[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].
- **Agent Communication & Protocols**: Protocols and client-server specifications for agent interactions.
- **Security & Observability**: Runtimes, guardrails, and telemetry tools for monitoring agent behavior.

# Lifecycle History
- Merged PR #18 added Higress (CNCF Sandbox AI Gateway) to Frameworks & Infrastructure → Orchestration & Multi-Agent[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Automated agentic workflow repository providing structured issue analysis skills, diagnostic triage schemas, and adversarial prompt injection test suites.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative providing automated triage and analytical skills for incoming repository issues and submissions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]. It defines standardized evaluation templates for classifying defect reports and feature requests, supported by an adversarial test fixture suite to validate model resilience against prompt injection attacks and malicious payload delivery [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Issue Analysis Schema

The issue analysis skill enforces a structured Markdown output contract designed to deliver concise, non-speculative diagnostic reports for maintainers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:

- **Summary:** A single-paragraph restatement of the reported issue in maintainer-oriented terminology [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Classification:** Categorization across three discrete axes:
  - *Type:* `bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  - *Severity:* `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational` with an explicit impact and workaround rationale [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  - *Reproducibility:* `reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, or `not-applicable` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Affected Components:** Explicit file paths or module references rather than abstract functional labels [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Root-Cause Hypotheses:** Proposed technical mechanisms accompanied by specific criteria to confirm or refute them [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Suggested Actions:** Prioritized diagnostics, code inspection steps, and targeted inquiries rather than unverified patches [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Open Questions & Related Reviews:** Specific follow-ups for the issue reporter and historical cross-references to inform the triage [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

### Security and Injection Testing Fixtures

To ensure robustness against malicious input received via public issue trackers, the repository incorporates evaluation fixtures simulating prompt injection and evasive payloads [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60]:

- **Instruction Overrides & Exfiltration:** Direct attempts to override system prompts, alter persona constraints, and exfiltrate internal system instructions or tool definitions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Obfuscation Techniques:** Multi-layered evasion incorporating Base64 encodings, ROT13 ciphers, and Cyrillic homoglyph lookalikes designed to bypass naive keyword filters [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Notification and Mention Floods:** Injected mass mentions (`@everyone`, Discord/channel user IDs) designed to abuse downstream notification workflows when raw titles are echoed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
- **Fabricated Tool Responses:** Synthetic tool-call blocks (`tool_call`, `<invoke>`) and fake success payloads attempting to spoof execution state and trigger unauthorized side effects [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].

# Related Initiatives

- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md)
- [Public Agents](../initiatives/public-agents.md)
- [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../policies/working-group-submission-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Automated agentic workflow repository providing structured issue analysis skills, diagnostic triage, and prompt injection resilience testing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an Agentic AI Foundation initiative providing automated agent workflows and specialized skills to triage, analyze, and diagnose incoming GitHub issue submissions and pull requests across foundation repositories. In addition to performing diagnostic issue evaluation and metadata tagging, the initiative maintains robust defenses and validation suites to detect and withstand adversarial prompt injection attempts embedded in untrusted community contributions.

# Architecture / Specification

The project incorporates an automated test fixture suite covering common prompt injection vectors and adversarial manipulation techniques targeted at automated triage agents:

- **Environment Variable Exfiltration**: Direct and encoded requests instructing the triage agent to expose sensitive runtime configuration secrets, such as API tokens and service account keys [^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Hidden Markup Instructions**: Adversarial directives concealed inside HTML comments designed to manipulate severity classification, suppress injection detection flags, or forge review approvals [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Untrusted Remote Resource Fetching**: Payloads prompting the triage agent to download and evaluate arbitrary external links or execute remote scripts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Invisible Character and Role-Play Manipulation**: Payloads combining Unicode control characters and persona-hijack instructions to bypass content policies or force predetermined triage resolutions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- **Nested Formatting and HTML Script Injection**: Submissions leveraging collapsed HTML details blocks, image error handlers, and nested mentions to subvert parsing layers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].
- **Authority Impersonation and Urgency Coercion**: Social engineering prompts simulating governance authority demands to override core instructions under threat of compliance penalties [^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].

These adversarial evaluation patterns align with security controls defined in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md).

# References

- Test Fixture Suite: `tests/fixtures/injections/` in the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].
