proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, empirical surveys, and architectural practices for agent accuracy and reliability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation developing open standards, evaluation criteria, empirical surveys, and architectural practices to measure and improve AI agent accuracy, correctness, and operational dependability[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

## Working Group Scope & Deliverables
The working group investigates failure modes, reliability factors, quality evidence, and mitigation patterns across real-world agentic deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Key deliverables include:
- **AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey:** A standardized 16-question platform-neutral survey instrument gathering empirical data on real-world AI deployment stages (pilot, limited deployment, broad deployment), human-in-the-loop verification, failure consequences, frequency of unacceptable results, and shared industry priorities[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Taxonomy Representation:** Domain Editors Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam represent the working group in the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define and shepherd accuracy and reliability terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Lifecycle History
The ARWG conducts open public meetings under the Technical Committee governance, regularly reviewing community deliverables and cross-workgroup contributions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working-group workstream curating a unified SKOS-Lite taxonomy and ecosystem market map across AAIF domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream maintains the horizontal, shared vocabulary and ecosystem market map across all active technical working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]. The workstream operates under a multi-stakeholder governance model where terminology definitions are standardized in a SKOS-Lite-compliant schema to prevent siloed or conflicting vocabularies across domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

While the market landscape mapping is positioned on the future roadmap, active contribution is currently constrained strictly to the taxonomy glossary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance Roles
Repository curation is partitioned across three core roles[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]:
- **Contributors**: Open community members and working group participants who propose terms and file issues via git PRs or issue templates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
- **Domain Editors**: Technical delegates from the seven active Technical Working Groups who author, review, and curate domain entries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
- **Maintainers / Workstream Chairs**: Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic, who hold repository write access and execute final administrative merges[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

## Review Process and Acceptance Criteria
All proposed terms must adhere to strict acceptance standards before inclusion[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]:
1. **Cross-WG Review**: A pull request requires review and approval by at least two or three Domain Editors from distinct Technical Working Groups (spanning both the originating WG and an adjacent group like [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) or [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md))[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
2. **Scope Alignment**: Terms must be cross-cutting (affecting $\ge$ 2 WGs) or foundational to the entire foundation; single-WG specialized terminology resides in individual WG repositories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
3. **Neutrality and Precision**: Entries must remain vendor-neutral, pre-competitive, and technically bounded[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
4. **Anti-Erasure Guardrails**: True synonyms are added to the `aliases` property of an existing entry only with written sign-off from the owning Domain Editor; distinct conceptual variants must be retained as discrete entries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

proposed_concept.description: Visual identity standards, design tokens, typography specifications, and document formatting rules for AAIF assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines establish the visual identity standards, design tokens, surface specifications, and typography policies governing official foundation assets, collateral, and document generation workflows[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification

## Design Tokens and Asset Rendering
Core visual variables are maintained live in `design/aaif-tokens.css`, defining canonical ink, paper, and hairline color tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Chapter badging and scene graphics dynamically consume tokens to ensure deterministic styling across collateral, utilizing headless Chrome as the approved rendering engine[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

## Typography and Font Embedding Policies
For OOXML (`.docx`) and Google Docs workflows, typography enforces explicit declaration and embedding rules to minimize document bloat while guaranteeing typographic consistency[^evt-community-events-pr-34]:
- **Declared but Unembedded (`ox.NEVER_EMBED`)**: Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono are declared in document style tables but stripped of embedded font binaries, relying on cloud runtime availability in Google Docs[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback Embedding**: Manrope is retained as an embedded metric fallback font to preserve layout geometry in environments lacking local Instrument Sans support[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Typographic Split**: Body and prose runs render in Instrument Sans, whereas field labels, table headers, dates, owners, and status indicators are formatted in JetBrains Mono[^evt-community-events-pr-34].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity standards, design tokens, typography specifications, and document formatting rules for AAIF digital and presentation assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual identity standards, core design tokens, typography specifications, color palettes, and automated compliance rules across all Foundation digital, documentation, and office presentation assets[^evt-community-events-pr-32]. All official publications, community slide templates, and OOXML documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel) must conform to central design tokens to maintain consistent visual hierarchy, vendor neutrality, and legibility[^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Typography
AAIF standardizes typography across web, documentation, and Office/OOXML formats:
- **Primary Typeface**: Instrument Sans is the standard display and theme font across all decks, documents, and tracker body copy, replacing legacy fonts (such as Space Grotesk, Manrope, Arial, JetBrains Mono, and Calibri)[^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Embedding and Fallbacks**: While web platforms consume web fonts (such as WOFF2), OOXML document pipelines reconcile `word/fontTable.xml` and prune unreferenced embedded font binaries to avoid artifact bloat and font substitution distortion[^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Palette and Design Tokens
Visual styling is managed through role-aware design token mappings rather than hardcoded hex values or stock office software defaults[^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Neutrals and Inks**: Neutral styling applies AAIF token scales including `--line-2`, `--ink-4`, and `--ink-3` for borders, secondary copy, and metadata[^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Accent Spectrum**: Highlighting and status indicators utilize spectrum tokens such as `--spec-3`[^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Plate and Table Formatting**: Dark plate / black plate headers with hairline borders replace legacy navy fills[^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Role-Aware Application**: Document automation pipelines distinguish XML color context so that fill tokens and border tokens apply correctly without blind find-and-replace corruptions[^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Contrast and Legibility Verification
To prevent unreadable asset combinations (such as dark ink on black plates), automated validation checks calculate the rendered fill against underlying background hierarchies (shape fill → slide background → layout → master → canvas white) to enforce strict contrast compliance before asset distribution[^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Hosted Projects Template Identity
Standard presentation templates (such as chapter About slides) must display the current roster of hosted AAIF projects: `MCP · goose · AGENTS.md · agentgateway · A2A · Agent Router`[^evt-community-events-pr-46]. Template sweeps automatically adjust text bounding boxes and font sizing to maintain visual balance across standardized slides without text collisions or orphaned labels[^evt-community-events-pr-46].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Job-oriented reference architecture enabling constrained agent iteration on fenced tasks with deterministic gates, activity-level boundaries, and recovery policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an AAIF reference architecture that operationalizes constrained autonomous agent iteration within strictly demarcated problem domains and runtime fences [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]. It pairs probabilistic proposal generation with deterministic acceptance gates to remediate localized technical faults without unbounded loop execution.

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture formalizes execution boundaries by explicitly distinguishing between workflow subunits and domain-level task scopes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]:

- **Business Task**: The bounded business problem or work item admitted to and resolved by an end-to-end execution run [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Activity**: Granular, discrete workflow subunits executed within the broader remediation pipeline [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

Remediation pipelines compose foundational primitives including the [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), and [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) across admission, convergence, validation, and recovery lifecycles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #49**: Clarified business task terminology versus activity-level workflow subunits across lifecycle stages, gate evaluations, and recovery mechanisms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skill Evaluation Methodology
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation framework for agent skills combining dual-arm delta testing, trigger space disambiguation, and behavioral guardrail validation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Skill Evaluation Methodology provides a targeted empirical framework for verifying that conversational AI agents correctly trigger and adhere to modular skill definitions [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]. Unlike deterministic structural checks (such as YAML validation or unit tests), skill evaluation assesses probabilistic model behavior against prompt triggers and negative edge cases [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation harness implements several core testing strategies:

- **Dual-Arm Differential Testing**: Runs evaluation cases twice—once with the skill bundle active and once without [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]. Graders marked `arm: with-only` measure the delta ($\Delta$) contributed specifically by the skill instructions over the base model's default behavior [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **Trigger Disambiguation and Negative Selection**: Evaluates prompts that sit close in semantic description space to ensure the target skill fires [^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76] while strictly forbidding neighboring sibling skills from executing (`not_the_neighbours`) [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d] [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6].
- **Behavioral and Safety Guardrails**: Validates that skills enforce required operational boundaries, such as preventing PII leakage in public biographies or refusing adversarial manipulation from untrusted intake inputs [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **Credential and Environment Isolation**: Separates model-driven evaluations from automated uncredentialed CI runs to avoid exposing model API secrets on untrusted pull requests [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

# References

- Community Events Skill Evaluation Suite [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]
- Public Agent Resources and Skills in [Public Agents](../initiatives/public-agents.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing telemetry standards, distributed trace models, semantic conventions, and cross-boundary verification for AI agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open standards, reference architectures, semantic conventions, and instrumentation practices for observing and verifying autonomous agent workflows and distributed multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

Key areas of work include trace attestation, lineage tracking, runtime verification, cross-boundary telemetry, and standardizing agent behavioral capture across heterogeneous infrastructures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Architecture / Specification

### Agent Behavior Trace Model
The group is driving an execution plan for an Agent Behavior Trace Model designed to correlate probabilistic agent cognition with observable deterministic execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Core relational capabilities include:
- **Model Calls and Retries:** Associating failed and successful model attempts with triggering work units without double-counting usage or creating fictional execution records[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Approvals:** Linking human-in-the-loop and policy decisions explicitly to proposed actions, preserving clear boundaries between requested actions and verified authorizations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **External Effects:** Correlating internal agent tool invocations with independently observed downstream service mutations and receipts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

### Cross-Boundary Observability & Registry Integration
The working group evaluates cross-boundary telemetry models linking registries, routers, and runtime agents using W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25]. Potential integration pathways include Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) and agent identity protocols to address multi-domain observability challenges[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-16:** Working group review advanced the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution roadmap, established cross-boundary observability proposals, and coordinated monthly APAC regional synchronization[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# References

- Related Architecture: [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md)
- Related Pattern: [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)
- Related Taxonomy: [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skill Evaluation Guideline
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation framework and trigger verification methodology for agent skills, portable tools, and prompt descriptions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Skill Evaluation Guideline provides standard procedures and testing harnesses for verifying that modular agent skills, portable tools, and MCP servers trigger reliably, execute deterministically, and preserve safety guarantees[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759][^evt-community-events-pr-47].

Skill evaluation pairs programmatic runtime validation with behavioral trigger testing to ensure agent skill descriptions reliably activate on realistic user requests rather than only verbatim description echoes[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

# Architecture / Specification

### Skill Activation and Trigger Testing
Trigger evaluation measures whether the model invokes a target skill given a realistic natural-language prompt[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]:
- **Realistic Inquiries:** Prompts must reflect authentic user queries instead of mirroring the exact terminology of the skill's manifest or docstring[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].
- **Description Compression Verification:** When skill descriptions are shortened or optimized for context limits, trigger graders evaluate whether the skill retains its activation fidelity[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].
- **Grading Constraints:** Tests check for explicit tool invocation tokens matching skill names and argument patterns[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

### Drift Prevention and Portable Plumbing
To ensure portable skills execute cleanly across environments, libraries enforce structural hygiene[^evt-community-events-pr-47]:
- **Drift Guards:** Enforcing byte-identical safety banners, legal disclaimers, and redaction flags across distributed standalone skills[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Error Classification:** Distinguishing permanent non-retryable operational errors from transient infrastructure faults in client wrappers[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09:** Standardized skill firing evaluation harness and automated drift checks incorporated into portable community agent repositories[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759][^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# References

- Related Initiative: [Public Agents](../initiatives/public-agents.md)
- Related Working Group: [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Observability architecture specifying context propagation, span ownership, and telemetry capture across the Agent-to-Tool semantic boundary realized via local CLI subprocesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary reference architecture formalizes observability across the transition between an agent execution runtime and local CLI tool subprocesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It distinguishes the canonical semantic Agent-to-Tool interaction from the operational Agent Runtime to Local Process boundary that executes it [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification
The realization maps eight cross-boundary observability dimensions across execution layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]:
- **Context Propagation**: Employs W3C Trace Context and W3C Baggage propagated through process boundaries using the OpenTelemetry environment-variable context carrier specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Ownership and Composition**: Coordinates `execute_tool` spans from the agent runtime with subprocess CLI caller spans. Pre-execution span-ID reservation enables child processes to attach telemetry deterministically to runtime-managed parent contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Asynchronous Execution**: Distinguishes synchronous child invocations from detached or background jobs, linking the latter via OpenTelemetry Span Links rather than strict parent-child nesting [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Evidence Integrity**: Treats telemetry authenticity as a cross-cutting concern to reconcile declared tool actions against independent operational telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

This architecture integrates with standard OpenTelemetry pipelines defined in [OpenTelemetry SDK Instrumentation](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) and relates to foundational definitions in [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# References
- [AAIF Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Chapter Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy establishing a 100-chapter hard ceiling, defined lifecycle states, and Slack organizer synchronization procedures for AAIF community chapters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Chapter Lifecycle Policy governs the provisioning, capacity constraints, status tracking, and retirement of regional AAIF community chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. The policy caps the total chapter estate at a hard limit of 100 chapters, requiring growth beyond this threshold to be offset by merging or deprecating dormant chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
The chapter lifecycle is managed through explicit human-curated status designations and automated membership synchronization [^evt-community-events-pr-48]:
- **Lifecycle Statuses**: Chapters transition across `Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, and `Deprecated` states. Merged chapters specify an associated target chapter via a companion reference field [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Estate Ceiling**: A maximum capacity limit of 100 registered chapters is enforced at intake and synchronization boundaries [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Organizer Room Synchronization**: Community organizer membership in the workspace-wide `#local-champs` channel is synchronized automatically against accepted organizer rosters [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Activity Audit Heuristics**: Chapter health evaluations rely strictly on positive communication signals (such as dated human messages) rather than absence of recorded events or synthetic metadata timestamps [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# References
- [Project Lifecycle Policy](../governance/project-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)

mutations.rationale: Introduce the working group gap model for treating control-plane telemetry as independent evidence to verify agent runtime self-reports.

proposed_concept.title: Control-Plane Telemetry Evidence Model
proposed_concept.description: Measurement framework modeling independent gateway, proxy, and runtime boundary observations to corroborate or contradict agent-emitted execution claims.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Control-Plane Telemetry Evidence Model establishes semantic foundations for evaluating independent boundary signals (from gateways, proxies, and runtime sandboxes) against self-reported agent telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]. Because agent-emitted traces may be misconfigured or unverified, external boundary observations provide independent corroboration or contradiction of executed actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework evaluates evidence value across two orthogonal dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:
- **Observation Source**: Identifies where the telemetry originated, including agent runtimes, tool execution environments, network gateways/proxies, or external third-party systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
- **Observation Relationship**: Classifies the semantic claim of the signal relative to the agent's asserted action as direct observation, corroborating evidence, contradictory evidence, or derived telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

Reconciliation produces three distinct operational states: `agreement`, `contradiction`, or `no independent evidence` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]. The absence of independent boundary observation is treated as an explicit measurement state rather than implicit confirmation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

This evidence model integrates with cross-boundary observability matrices defined in [AAIF Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and security baselines in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skill Evaluation Framework
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation framework and trigger verification methodology for agent skills, portable tools, and multi-skill orchestration pipelines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Skill Evaluation Framework defines empirical verification patterns, trigger fidelity tests, and multi-grader evaluation criteria for portable tools and agent skills within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem. It establishes testing standards to verify that agents correctly route high-level user requests to root orchestration skills rather than premature phase-specific skills, execute multi-stage operational pipelines in strict dependency order, separate reporting from destructive state writes, and comply with mandatory output requirements such as legal footers[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a][^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5][^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].

# Architecture / Specification

### Trigger Disambiguation and Namespace Isolation

When multiple specialized phase skills (for example, `aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, and `aaif-sync-slack`) share semantic overlap with a general front-door orchestrator (`aaif-sync`), evaluations must enforce strict routing boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]:

1. **Positive Tool Triggering (`tool_used`)**: High-level or estate-wide operational prompts must invoke the top-level orchestrator skill that manages end-to-end pipeline execution and sequencing[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
2. **Negative Trace Assertions (`not_contains`)**: The evaluation harness asserts via trace inspection regexes that no individual phase skill fires independently for an estate-level prompt, preventing partial or incomplete pipeline runs[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

### Grader Typology

The evaluation harness employs three complementary grader types:

- **Regex Graders**: Perform deterministic matching over final outputs or traces. Used to verify structural compliance, such as ensuring attendee-facing announcements carry both mandatory links (`../policies/code-of-conduct.md` and Privacy Policy) to prevent legal footer drift[^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].
- **Tool Invocations Graders**: Assert minimum tool usage counts and match tool parameters or skill names within execution traces[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
- **Model-Based Evaluators (LLM Graders)**: Evaluate behavioral ordering, ensuring the agent proposes multi-stage actions as ordered dependency sequences, generates review reports prior to mutations, and adheres to `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md` by confirming candidate matches before mutating downstream state[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

- Proposal-Execution Split: `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`
- Code of Conduct: `../policies/code-of-conduct.md`

proposed_concept.title: Community Chapter Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy establishing chapter lifecycle states, spreadsheet configuration schemas, and Slack channel mapping and synchronization rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Chapter Lifecycle Policy governs the creation, operation, auditing, and retirement of local AAIF community chapters. Chapter configuration, room mapping, and metadata are maintained directly in the live AAIF Community Chapters List spreadsheet rather than static repository files, enabling chapter organizers and operations leads to maintain directory state without submitting pull requests[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]. Automated synchronization skills read this configuration to audit channel coverage, align membership, and stage infrastructure updates[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd][^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Chapter Configuration Schema

Channel matching and audit behavior for `aaif-audit-slack` and `aaif-sync-slack` are driven by dedicated columns in the AAIF Community Chapters List[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:

- `Slack Channel`: Explicit public channel override for non-standard slugs (e.g., mapping San Francisco to `bay-area`). Blank cells trigger prefix/suffix scanning; the sentinel `none` indicates no channel exists and halts heuristic guessing[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- `Organizer Channel`: Explicit leads channel override where standard `<city>-organizers` naming is not used[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- `Country Channel`: Regional or national rooms (e.g., `india` or `africa`). Reported strictly as regional coverage and never counted as dedicated local chapter presence[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- `Ops Notes`: Free-text human operational context quoted in health reports but never programmatically acted upon[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

### Matching Precedence and Vocabulary

Vocabulary rules live on the `Slack Config` tab of the spreadsheet, where row order is load-bearing[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:

- **Public Channel Prefixes**: Evaluated top-to-bottom starting with `(none)` (bare city slug), followed by prefixes such as `meetup-`, `aaif-`, `mlops-`, and `aaif`[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Organizer Channel Suffixes**: Evaluated top-to-bottom as `<city><suffix>` (`-organizers`, `-organisers`, `-chapter-leads`, `-organizer`, `-leads`, `-meetup-organizers`)[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Staff Email Domains**: Identifies foundation staff accounts to avoid classifying them as unmapped regular members[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

### Operational Safety Invariants

1. **Reports Precede Writes**: Audit reports and candidate proposals must always be generated and reviewed before mutating spreadsheet cells, Drive permissions, or Slack state[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
2. **No Auto-Mapping Aliases**: Automated sync scripts only write exact channel name matches. Candidate aliases or near-misses must be proposed to human operators for explicit confirmation[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

# References

- Agent Skill Evaluation Framework: `../guidelines/agent-skill-evaluation.md`
- Code of Conduct: `../policies/code-of-conduct.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model Contract
proposed_concept.description: Shared identity and relationship trace contract specifying execution primitives, turn-boundary rules, and interpretation invariants for agent behavior observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model contract defines a standardized identity and relationship specification for capturing, correlating, and interpreting behavioral telemetry across agentic workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the contract establishes a vendor-neutral schema spanning agent conversations, model invocations, governance gates, and external side effects.

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model organizes agent execution telemetry around eight discrete identity primitives and six structural relationships [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:

- **Identities**:
  - `Conversation`: Top-level interaction thread between human users, systems, or coordinating agents.
  - `Runtime Session`: Execution container or host process lifecycle hosting agent operations.
  - `Turn`: Discrete processing cycle bounded by turn-boundary rules.
  - `Model Call`: Inference request and response interaction with foundation model providers.
  - `Proposed Action`: Intent or tool invocation formulated probabilistically by the agent prior to execution.
  - `Approval Decision`: Human or policy gate determination authorizing, rejecting, or modifying a proposed action.
  - `Tool Execution`: Concrete invocation and execution of a tool or function.
  - `External Effect`: Side-effect modification observed in external systems or environments.

- **Interpretation Invariants**:
  - *Missing observations*: Telemetry gaps represent unknown states rather than zero occurrences [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
  - *Deduplication*: Duplicate events are deduplicated deterministically via explicit correlation keys [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
  - *Order independence*: Out-of-order event arrivals must not alter behavioral state interpretations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

- **Crosswalks & Compatibility**:
  - Direct mapping to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] (see [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md)).
  - Harmonization with AAIF core workflow terminology [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] (see [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)).

# Lifecycle History
The v0.1 draft specification was submitted in working-documents PR #51 to WG Observability and Traceability, serving as an intake contract to be evaluated against empirical baseline traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability and Traceability) develops vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing standards, and runtime profiling architectures for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agent systems. The group standardizes behavioral trace models, context propagation protocols, and cross-layer telemetry correlation spanning kernel, userspace, and model boundaries.

# Key Initiatives and Specifications
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A shared behavioral trace contract specifying identities (conversations, sessions, turns, model calls, proposed actions, approval decisions, tool executions, external effects), interpretation invariants, and crosswalks to OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] (see [Agent Behavior Trace Model Contract](../proposals/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)).
- **Agent-Tool CLI Boundary**: Observability standards for tracing tool execution and subshell context across CLI boundaries (see [Agent Tool CLI Boundary](../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md)).
- **Cross-Layer Tracing**: Integration architectures bridging kernel probes, userspace tracepoints, and GPU execution profiling (see [LTTng UST](../reference-architectures/lttng-ust.md), [GPU AI Tracing](../reference-architectures/gpu-ai-tracing.md), and [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md)).

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #51**: Introduced the v0.1 draft contract for the Agent Behavior Trace Model, establishing core identity primitives, turn-boundary definitions, and telemetry interpretation invariants [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group initiative responsible for developing and maintaining a unified SKOS-Lite terminology taxonomy and an interactive landscape map for the agentic AI ecosystem. The workstream reviews proposed terminology from technical committee submissions and working groups to ensure consistent definitions across AAIF specifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Operations and Tooling
- **Monthly Reporting**: The workstream submits monthly progress reports to the Technical Committee detailing terminology reviews, backlog processing, and schema definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **Taxonomy Validation CI**: Automated validation workflows (`validate-taxonomy.yml`) verify taxonomy data files using Node.js validator test suites [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].
- **Compute and Abuse Protection**: CI validation is gated behind trusted maintainer reviews (`pull_request_review`) and manual dispatch (`workflow_dispatch`), enforcing bounded runtime timeouts and concurrency controls to prevent resource exhaustion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Secured charter approvals, defined data schemas, and launched web portal pipelines [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **July 2026**: Reviewed 46 backlog terms and admitted 13 in the workstream's initial taxonomy pull request [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **August 2026**: Completed review of 53 terms (retaining 37) across three syncs and prepared four pull requests for Technical Committee approval [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared telemetry and trace contract specifying execution primitives, turn-boundary semantics, and causal relationship correlation for agent workflows in OpenTelemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and tracing specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to track AI agent activities across conversation turns, execution interruptions, and distributed system boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The contract maps AAIF agent execution concepts to [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) conventions, capturing causal relationships across model calls, retries, approvals, tool invocations, and external system effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model standardizes how agent execution contexts are recorded and queried by independent readers without accessing private agent internal state [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

## Validation Scenarios and Core Questions
The trace specification addresses four core observability questions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity**: Determining which interaction turns belong together across pauses, restarts, and trace context propagation.
- **Calls and Retries**: Correlating language model calls and retry attempts to specific turns without duplicate counting.
- **Approvals**: Linking human or policy approval decisions directly to proposed actions and tracking whether execution proceeded.
- **Effects**: Associating independently recorded external mutations with the responsible tool invocation.

## Execution and Implementation Roadmap
The nine-task execution plan guides implementation and upstream OpenTelemetry alignment [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]:
1. **Execution Plan**: Formal roadmap definition and milestone breakdown.
2. **Baseline Examples**: Common scenario definitions using [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) and an independent agent runtime.
3. **Shared Contract**: Specification of identity models, turn boundaries, and entity relationships.
4. **Shared Test Harness**: Sample records, assertions, and contributor gap templates.
5. **Session and Turn Correlation**: Multi-trace continuity preserving existing caller contexts.
6. **Calls, Approvals, and Effects**: Telemetry links connecting LLM provider spans, approval gates, and downstream side-effects.
7. **Independent Interpretation**: Dual-engine trace verification across edge cases such as delayed or out-of-order spans.
8. **Test Automation**: Runnable fixtures across agent runtimes and standalone LLM providers.
9. **Upstream Submissions**: Concrete semantic convention proposals for OpenTelemetry GenAI workgroups.

# Lifecycle History
The execution plan was agreed upon in August 2026 working group meetings and merged in September 2026 as the plan of record [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies within the Agentic AI Foundation to build unified standards for observing AI agent behavior, reasoning, and distributed execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The group focuses on aligning existing telemetry ecosystems, identifying gaps in distributed tracing, and producing vendor-neutral specifications and guidance in close collaboration with bodies such as [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group manages core technical deliverables and collaboration frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../proposals/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: A formal execution plan and relationship contract standardizing session continuity, turn boundaries, approval tracking, and side-effect correlation in OpenTelemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Prior Work Survey**: A continuous landscape mapping of agent observability tooling, runtime tracing libraries, and adjacent initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Use Cases Inventory**: Shared collection of practitioner requirements across debugging, auditing, evaluation, and operational monitoring [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Governance & Operations
- **Chairs**: Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco, Chair) and Matthew Lee (Datadog, Co-Chair), serving appointed terms from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Meetings**: Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via Zoom and LFX Platform [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Coordination**: Public mailing list (`wg-observability-traceability@lists.aaif.io`) and AAIF Discord community [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) body dedicated to standardizing workflow patterns, orchestration primitives, reference architectures, and enterprise use cases for agentic systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. The group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Structure and Work Streams
The working group organizes its technical activities into three dedicated work streams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Defines and evaluates reusable structural patterns and reference blueprints, including `../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`, `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`, and `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`.
- **Taxonomy**: Standardizes vocabulary and primitives curated in `../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md`, coordinating with the foundation-wide `../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` effort to prevent conflicting term definitions across working groups[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Scopes and prioritizes real-world enterprise agent scenarios and operational requirements for integration into business processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Cross-Group Alignment and Governance
The working group collaborates with other AAIF bodies to harmonize workflow patterns with broader foundation standards, contributing core design principles to `../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md` and operating under the oversight of the `../governance/technical-committee.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Evidence Record Specification
proposed_concept.description: Testable data model and schema standardizing tamper-evident agent execution records across observation, verification, integrity grades, and claim reconciliation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Evidence Record Specification is a testable data model and schema standardizing tamper-evident execution evidence for autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the format resolves the E4 use-case gap for evidence-grade trace interchange without binding implementations to specific vendor mechanisms.

# Architecture / Specification

The specification defines a JSON Schema and strict validator encoding four core dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]:

- **Observation**: Encodes the origin source (from agent self-reports to external authorities) and relationship types (direct, corroborating, contradictory, derived), aligning with the [Control Plane Telemetry Evidence Model](../guidelines/control-plane-telemetry-evidence-model.md).
- **Verification**: Formulates verification basis via orthogonal axes of vantage (substrate vs. artifact) and capture method (intercepted vs. reconstructed).
- **Grade Ladder**: Implements the E0–E4 progression (Declared, Observed, Enforced, Corroborated, Anchored) tied directly to strict integrity requirement floors.
- **Claims and Reconciliation**: Tracks emission-conformant and operationally-conformant assertions, evaluating multi-source alignment across a three-state model (agreement, contradiction, or absence of independent evidence).

The record model remains implementation-agnostic by recording integrity marker presence rather than enforcing proprietary cryptographic implementations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].

# Lifecycle History

Introduced in Observability & Traceability issue #37 alongside an open reference validator and fixture suite to facilitate schema fuzzing and cross-working-group interoperability testing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].

proposed_concept.title: Control Plane Telemetry Evidence Model
proposed_concept.description: Measurement framework modeling independent gateway, proxy, and runtime boundary observations to corroborate agent behavior against tamper-evident evidence records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Control Plane Telemetry Evidence Model establishes an independent verification framework that correlates agent runtime telemetry with external network gateway, sidecar proxy, and hardware boundary observations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]. By cross-referencing internal agent self-reporting with authoritative external control-plane telemetry, the framework provides verifiable corroboration of agent actions.

# Architecture / Specification

The model defines criteria for evaluating trace integrity and evidence grade [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]:

- **Vantage Points**: Contrasts internal artifact-level emissions with external substrate-level interception points.
- **Observation Relationships**: Classifies telemetry signals into direct, corroborating, contradictory, and derived evidence paths.
- **Evidence Interchange**: Standardizes data structures into canonical evidence records via the [Evidence Record Specification](../proposals/evidence-record-spec.md) to support three-state claim reconciliation across disparate observability systems.

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../proposals/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework organizing AAIF reference architectures around practitioner jobs, reusable patterns, and prospective machine-readable Workflow Design Specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Job-Oriented Architecture Model establishes a structural paradigm organizing AAIF reference architectures around recognizable practitioner operational jobs rather than abstract capabilities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]. It composes modular workflow design patterns with concrete validation scenarios to produce consistent and verifiable agentic system architectures.

# Architecture / Specification

The foundational architecture model operates across three complementary tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]:

1. **Reusable Patterns**: Atomic building blocks that resolve recurring workflow challenges, such as [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
2. **Job-Oriented Reference Architectures**: Compositions combining patterns, capability roles, trust boundaries, guarantees, and exit states to execute defined practitioner jobs (e.g., [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../reference-architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)).
3. **Real-World Scenarios**: Empirical use cases providing validation evidence and boundary testing for reference compositions.

### North-Star Evolution: Workflow Design Specification

The [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) is evaluating the long-term delivery artifact of the reference architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]:

- **Option A (Reusable Guidance)**: Reference architectures remain a knowledge base of patterns, compositions, and scenario validation rules, leaving concrete implementation formatting to practitioners.
- **Option B (Machine-Readable Workflow Design Specification)**: Reference architectures produce a versioned, schema-valid, machine-readable specification (WDS in YAML/JSON) from which diagrams, audit views, and implementation handoffs are derived.

# Lifecycle History

Originally formulated by the Reference Architectures Workstream, with expanded scope debated in issue #28 regarding the transition toward executable, schema-backed workflow specifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

proposed_concept.title: Hard Constraint Human Oversight
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern mandating permanent human execution or sign-off dictated by statutory, regulatory, or policy requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Hard Constraint Human Oversight pattern enforces mandatory human accountability checkpoints required by legal, regulatory, or institutional frameworks, regardless of the autonomous agent's capabilities or historical reliability [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. Unlike temporary trust-building gates (such as standard approval checkpoints), hard constraints are structural and non-negotiable [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

### Distinction from Temporary Approval Gates

In workflow architectures, oversight mechanisms often serve two distinct purposes:

1. **Confidence-Based Gates**: Implemented when an autonomous system is not yet fully trusted, designed to evolve over time into exception escalation or fully automated execution via autonomy graduation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
2. **Hard Constraints**: Implemented when law, clinical policy, or fiduciary standards mandate human agency and liability (for example, formal physician signatures, licensed attorney legal certifications, or board-level financial authorizations) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

### Invariant Rules

- **Exclusion from Graduation**: Systems undergoing autonomy graduation must explicitly exclude hard constraint checkpoints from automatic relaxation or bypass [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Immutable Auditability**: Hard constraint decisions must record the specific human identity, credential context, and explicit affirmation payload [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# Lifecycle History

Proposed in PR #42 within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to resolve ambiguity in human-in-the-loop pattern classifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References

- Related pattern: [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- Working Group: [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: Autonomy Graduation Lifecycle
proposed_concept.description: Operational progression guideline for evolving agent oversight from synchronous approval gates to exception escalation and unprompted execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Autonomy Graduation Lifecycle documents the staged progression of operational oversight as an agentic system demonstrates empirical reliability in production environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

### Graduation Stages

The typical progression moves across three discrete stages:

1. **Approval Gate**: Synchronous human review and authorization required for every candidate action or state transition [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
2. **Exception Escalation**: Autonomous execution proceeds by default within bounded operational parameters, escalating to human operators only when uncertainty boundaries or safety guards are triggered [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
3. **Full Autonomous Execution (None)**: Autonomous execution within defined environmental boundaries without routine human intervention [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

### Non-Graduating Invariants

Structural requirements designated under [Hard Constraint Human Oversight](../patterns/hard-constraint-human-oversight.md) are strictly excluded from the graduation lifecycle and must remain intact regardless of reliability metrics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References

- [Hard Constraint Human Oversight](../patterns/hard-constraint-human-oversight.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)

# Overview

The PostHog reference architecture details client-side and server-side product analytics integration for tracking agent usage, adoption metrics, and interaction funnels [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

### Telemetry and Identity Considerations

- **Identifier Semantics**: Implementations frequently utilize persistent installation identifiers (e.g., random UUIDs) to trace longitudinal usage [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Jurisdictional Privacy Classification**: While often characterized as anonymous in US-centric contexts, persistent client identifiers constitute pseudonymous personal data under the EU GDPR (Recitals 26 and 30) and UK GDPR [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55]. proposed_concept.title: MCP Gateway & Registry
proposed_concept.description: Centralized control plane and catalog for discovering, proxying, and governing access to MCP servers, A2A agents, and reusable skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The MCP Gateway & Registry is an open-source platform designed to centralize and govern enterprise access to AI assets, specifically Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol agents, and reusable agent skills [^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]. It addresses credential sprawl, security blindspots, and integration overhead by acting as a single, governed control plane between AI development tools, coding assistants, autonomous agents, and backend tools.

# Architecture / Specification

The project implements four core functional layers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]:

1. **MCP Server Gateway**: A proxy providing single-point ingress to multiple MCP servers with fine-grained authorization at the tool and method level, virtual MCP server aggregation, and real-time observability.
2. **MCP Servers Registry**: Discovery and governance catalog implementing the upstream Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0.1 specification.
3. **Agent Registry & A2A Communication Hub**: Agent card registration and semantic search discovery for direct peer-to-peer agent-to-agent communication via the A2A protocol.
4. **Agent Skills Registry**: Catalog for versioned, reusable skills providing per-skill credential management and integrated security scanning.

### Security and Federation

The platform integrates with enterprise Identity Providers (Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Auth0, Amazon Cognito) for developer and machine-to-machine authentication [^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]. It incorporates automated security scanning for MCP servers, agents, and skills via Cisco AI Defense. The architecture supports three federation patterns:
- Peer-to-peer registry federation across autonomous enterprise instances.
- Upstream server sync with the Anthropic MCP Registry.
- Federation with AWS Agent Registry / Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

# Lifecycle History

Submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation under Apache 2.0 licensing, originating from community development in May 2025 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]. It is positioned as complementary to client-side agent runtimes such as [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) and repository context conventions like AGENTS.md, as well as data-plane proxy proposals.

# References

- [Agent-to-Agent Protocol and MCP Registry Proposal](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/29)
- [Goose Reference Architecture](../reference-architectures/goose.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../proposals/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)

# Overview

Nono is a reference architecture and implementation under evaluation within the Observability and Traceability Working Group for kernel-enforced sandboxing and low-level boundary telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]. It establishes deterministic security, provenance, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) boundary capture for autonomous agent execution environments.

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture provides concrete field references, golden trace vectors, and layer mappings spanning below-L7 execution boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]:

- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry Rows**: Standardized interaction mappings covering Agent-to-Gateway/Runtime, Agent-to-Human (HITL), and Agent-to-Tool interactions.
- **Kernel Enforcement Layer**: Classifies security isolation and policy enforcement across kernel, broker, and proxy layers, fitting the SAF-M-74 runtime class.
- **Trace Propagation Considerations**: Identifies trace context propagation mechanics (such as W3C `TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`, and `BAGGAGE` environment allow-lists) required to correlate kernel-level audit records with application-level OTLP spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning technical agentic architectures with global regulatory frameworks, compliance controls, and risk taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group aligns technical agentic architectures with international regulatory frameworks, statutory compliance obligations, and risk management best practices [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. The group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase).

# Architecture / Specification

The working group conducts comparative regulatory and gap analyses against a baseline of 16 core governance themes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:

1. **Governance & accountability**: Ownership, approvals, RACI frameworks, and risk acceptance.
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Prohibited vs. permitted systems and tiered control schemas.
3. **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundaries, and control placement.
4. **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication/authorization models, acting-on-behalf-of delegation, and registries.
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Business rules, policy-as-code enforcement, and operational constraints.
6. **Data protection & privacy**: PII management, data minimization, retention schedules, and data residency.
7. **Security & access controls**: Least privilege, secrets isolation, workload segmentation, and tool permissions.
8. **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, robustness benchmarks, drift detection, and change control.
9. **Human oversight**: HITL/HOTL escalation mechanisms, override/kill switches, and automated oversight.
10. **Action management**: Pre-execution checks, dual-control validation, and reversible operations.
11. **Monitoring & logging**: Audit trails, prompt/tool invocation logs, and deterministic decision logs.
12. **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection defense, tool abuse mitigations, and autonomy failure modes.
13. **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence, model weight provenance, and tool dependency tracking.
14. **Incident response**: Detection procedures, containment policies, and regulatory reporting triggers.
15. **Transparency & user disclosure**: AI interaction notices, explainability records, and user expectation framing.
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Statutory retention schedules, tamper-evident logs, and execution reproducibility.

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group established the 16-theme baseline and developed standardized extraction prompts for multi-jurisdictional policy comparisons [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# References

- [WG Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment August 2026 Report](https://github.com/aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory/blob/71b58c4f7fcc68f8001291436a75d8b0f60877e9/reporting/2026-08-report.md)

proposed_concept.title: Proposal-Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern strictly separating probabilistic intent generation and analysis from privileged execution through permission boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal-Execution Split is an architectural workflow pattern that strictly decouples probabilistic agent reasoning and artifact analysis from privileged mutation of production environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Instead of relying on internal LLM guardrails or direct runtime gates, isolation is enforced through separate job-level permissions, credential isolation, and deterministic validation stages.

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern structures agentic workflows into bounded, unprivileged stages followed by deterministic execution phases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:

- **Analysis Phase (Unprivileged)**: The agent operates in a constrained runtime equipped exclusively with read-only tools (e.g., Read, Grep, Glob) and read-scoped tokens. Shell, network, and write operations are strictly disallowed to isolate untrusted upstream inputs.
- **Sanitization & Artifact Handoff**: Analysis outputs are deterministically scanned (e.g., for verbatim credentials, malformed schemas, or policy violations) before being exported as static artifacts.
- **Execution Phase (Privileged)**: A separate, write-scoped deterministic job or human approver receives the verified artifact and applies the mutation (such as issue creation, pull request generation, or deployment).

```
[Trigger] --> [Read-Only Analysis Agent] --> [Artifact Scanner] --> [Privileged Execution Job]
```

# Lifecycle History

Cataloged by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group with production reference cases, including automated upstream SDK release impact analysis workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# References

- [Workflows and Process Integration Use Case Inventory PR #51](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/51)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate Pattern](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop Pattern](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security best practices, threat modeling frameworks, cross-WG review checklists, and design patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) establishes vendor-neutral security guidelines, threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and cross-working-group review processes for autonomous and agentic software systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. The group coordinates directly with peer AAIF working groups including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to address the attack surface and trust boundaries of agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs into distinct sub-workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: An actionable guideline cataloging architectural controls, static analysis heuristics, sandbox constraints, and operational controls for secure agent execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Threat Modeling Framework**: A gap analysis and framework design evaluating threat surfaces specific to multi-agent interactions, tool execution, and sandbox boundary bypasses[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Standardized patterns for hardware and microVM sandboxing, isolated execution runtimes, and policy enforcement points[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-Working-Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: A shared review matrix identifying security overlap, dependency management, and review sign-offs across AAIF initiatives and working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Contribution**: Curating and reviewing security-specific primitives within the shared AAIF terminology, supported by tooling tracking human edits versus LLM generation provenance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

## External Collaboration and Standards Alignment
The working group actively liaises with external standards and cybersecurity bodies:
- **ETSI TC SAI**: Tracking European Norm cybersecurity requirements for AI services and exploring bidirectional information exchange[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **OWASP & FINOS**: Monitoring the OWASP Agentic Top 10 and FINOS Open Enterprise Agent Governance efforts for compatibility[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Sandboxing Technologies**: Reviewing microVM-based agent sandboxes such as Eclipse Enclave for tighter kernel isolation and egress prevention[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-18**: Coordinated cross-boundary observability review with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), evaluated A2A donation implications, and initiated the cross-WG review checklist[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-09-15**: Finalized first-version review cutoffs for the [Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md), adopted quiet-period auto-merge policies for taxonomy PRs, and introduced taxonomy browser provenance tracking[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open telemetry standards, distributed trace models, semantic conventions, and use case frameworks for agent observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) develops vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents and multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra, the group surveys industry prior work, defines agent observability use cases, and standardizes cross-boundary telemetry across protocols like MCP, A2A, and OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Architecture / Specification

## Observability Landscape and Standards Integration
The working group maintains a continuous landscape survey analyzing industry specifications and tooling across key areas[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI**: Tracking semantic conventions across `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` for agent creation, invocation, workflow dispatch, and tool execution spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Protocol Telemetry**: Coordinating span context propagation and nested execution traces for Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and AGNTCY Observe SDK[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Security & Schema Normalization**: Aligning trace evidence with OCSF 1.9 (AI Agent, AI Operation, Delegation, and Record Integrity classes) and OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Environment Telemetry**: Complementing agent-emitted logs with eBPF-based runtime and network telemetry (e.g., OBI)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

## Use Case Framework and Cross-Cutting Requirements
The working group defines use cases across nine foundational operational categories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]:
1. **Debugging and Root Cause Analysis**: Reconstructing decision streams, context compaction, and loop detection (A1–A3).
2. **Cost Management and Optimization**: Token economics, cost attribution per outcome, and waste reduction (B1–B3).
3. **Code Attribution and Provenance**: Tracking AI-generated code and enabling security reviews (C1–C2).
4. **Evaluation and Quality Assurance**: Task regression benchmarks and multi-model evaluations (D1–D3).
5. **Safety and Compliance**: Scope boundaries, external actions, audit trails, and tamper-evident evidence records (E1–E4).
6. **Multi-Agent Systems**: Context propagation across boundaries and agent-to-agent delegation traces (F1–F2).
7. **Operational Monitoring**: Real-time health signals, SLIs/SLOs, and capacity planning (G1–G2).
8. **Research and Improvement**: Failure mode discovery, dataset generation, and replay trajectories (H1–H3).
9. **Identity and Ownership**: Cross-surface identity resolution across execution environments (I1).

### Foundational Telemetry Principles
All telemetry specifications developed by the group adhere to core criteria[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
- **Source and Trust**: Disambiguating self-reported agent data from independent host, proxy, sandbox, or network boundary observations.
- **Privacy and Governance**: Enforcing data minimization, credential redaction, access control, and retention policies directly within telemetry metadata.
- **Causality and Non-Linear Ordering**: Preserving causal links across asynchronous, queued, and multi-agent delegation chains without relying solely on wall-clock timestamps or single-tree span hierarchies.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-15**: Established working group landscape survey and use case inventory documents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **2026-08-13**: Completed mid-2026 landscape refresh documenting OTel GenAI repository split, A2A standardization, and OCSF 1.9 agent profile additions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-18**: Formally integrated tamper-evident evidence use cases (E4) and cross-boundary framework coordination with peer working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **2026-08-19**: Incorporated cross-surface identity resolution (I1) into the core use case matrix[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow models, common execution primitives, reference architectures, and taxonomy for multi-step agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops vendor-neutral workflow models, operational reference architectures, architectural principles, and core taxonomy for orchestrating agentic AI systems within enterprise processes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables across three primary workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:
- **Taxonomy:** Standardizes foundational terminology (such as "activity" and "workflow") in [../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md) while scoping out domain-specific gate/check terms to partner working groups.
- **Reference Architectures:** Builds and validates modular reference blueprints, including human-approved operations and bounded autonomous remediation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Evaluation uses a four-outcome architectural fit matrix: `validated`, `partial`, `candidate`, and `no fit` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Critical Use Cases:** Curates concrete enterprise inventory cases and validates architectural alignments against agreed taxonomy primitives [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group shipped the Phase One Core Terms draft following plenary approval, marking the first completed asset delivered across all AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The deliverable scope for reference architectures was finalized to include two reference blueprints, core architecture principles, and a contributor guide, enforcing a standing review policy that caps future pull requests at approximately ten files [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
