proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terminology
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary and foundational execution primitives defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group for multi-step agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Core Workflow Terminology defines the standardized vocabulary and execution primitives established by the [../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to describe agentic operations, state transitions, and orchestration boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. It provides unambiguous conceptual building blocks for reference architectures and use-case catalogs across the AAIF ecosystem.

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy establishes foundational hierarchical relationships and strict boundary definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:
- **Activity:** The foundational unit of work, defined independently without referencing workflow structures to eliminate circular dependency definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Workflow:** Defined strictly as an orchestration or composition of multiple activities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Lifecycle Semantics:** Adopts "lifecycle" terminology to replace vendor-specific "execution engine" references across architectural specifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Scope Boundaries:** Terminology specifically for gates, checks, and evaluations is explicitly scoped out of the workflow vocabulary and reserved for the Security, Observability, and Accuracy & Reliability working groups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History
The Phase One Core Terms draft was reviewed and formally voted through at the August 2026 plenary of the Workflows & Process Integration WG, becoming the first formal artifact delivered by an AAIF working group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Initial upstream alignment with the cross-working-group taxonomy workstream established agreement on six core terms while maintaining agentic-AI-specific domain definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared telemetry and trace contract specifying execution primitives, turn-boundary semantics, and causal evidence structures across autonomous agent frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and tracing specification developed by the [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture structured, causal evidence of agent deliberation, tool invocation, and side-effect outcomes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It provides standardized schema definitions ensuring traces generated by diverse agent runtimes can be independently reconstructed and validated without reliance on private runtime state.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines execution trace records, causal links between proposals and external effects, and strict interoperability verification rules [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:
- **Independent Interpretation:** Demonstrating interoperability requires at least two independently implemented readers or query paths to parse telemetry exports from multiple distinct agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Zero Private State Requirement:** Readers must reconstruct trace meaning without access to proprietary runtime state, hidden test fixtures, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Arrival Order Robustness:** Reconstructed causal graphs must correctly identify proposals, observed executions, and independently confirmed external effects regardless of telemetry delivery order [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Resilience to Incomplete Evidence:** If underlying confirmation receipts are missing or conflicting, readers must consistently report downstream effects as unconfirmed rather than generating erroneous state assertions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History
The trace model is tracked under a nine-task execution plan within the Observability & Traceability Working Group, with independent interpretation verification defined as Task 7 following the August 2026 working group sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: OpenSandbox
proposed_concept.description: General-purpose sandbox platform providing unified execution APIs, multi-language SDKs, an MCP server, and container/microVM isolation for agentic workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenSandbox is an open-source, general-purpose sandbox platform submitted as an AAIF project proposal to provide isolated execution substrates for AI-generated code, coding agents, GUI/browser agents, and evaluation workflows [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26]. Originally developed by Alibaba Group, it provides standardized lifecycle and command execution APIs alongside multi-language SDKs, container/microVM isolation backends, and an MCP server interface [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].

# Architecture / Specification
OpenSandbox provides execution and control plane primitives designed to isolate agent actions without forcing every agent framework to maintain bespoke sandboxing infrastructure [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26]:
- **Unified Lifecycle & Execution APIs:** Endpoints for creating, listing, inspecting, renewing, pausing, snapshotting, and deleting sandboxes, as well as executing shell commands, code blocks, filesystem operations, and streaming metrics [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **Isolation Options:** Runtime backends supporting standard Docker and Kubernetes controllers, with hardened microVM and secure container isolation via gVisor, Kata Containers, and Firecracker [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **MCP Integration:** An `opensandbox-mcp` server exposing sandbox management, command execution, and file I/O tools to Model Context Protocol clients [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **Multi-Language SDKs:** Client bindings spanning Python, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#/.NET, and Go [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **Network Governance:** Per-sandbox ingress and egress network filtering policies to restrict outbound exfiltration or unauthorized calls [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].

# Lifecycle History
The proposal was submitted to AAIF in May 2026 under the Apache 2.0 license, referencing integrations with tools such as [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) and coding agents [^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open telemetry standards, distributed trace models, semantic conventions, and cross-boundary execution observability across agent stacks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability (O&T) Working Group establishes open telemetry standards, distributed trace models, semantic conventions, and evaluation methods for tracking execution, context propagation, and reasoning trajectories across agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and Matthew Lee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives across several focus tracks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../proposals/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** Specification and portable context reference implementation linking plans, turn boundaries, decisions, and execution outcomes across heterogeneous SDKs and runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Defining standardized telemetry metadata and mapping conventions for agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Trust Pipeline:** Prototyping lifecycle tracing spanning discovery, identity/trust verification via Agent Gateway, and skill execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Taxonomy Contributions:** Curating formal O&T definitions including Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability into the shared AAIF taxonomy [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the WG confirmed the initial trace model scope, consolidated the Multi-Agentic Orchestration & Coordination focus group into the full working group, and established cross-WG liaisons across external bodies like OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG and internal AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared telemetry and trace contract specifying portable execution context, causal linking, turn boundaries, and decision metadata without requiring raw chain-of-thought capture.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a proposal developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) establishing portable telemetry context and execution primitives to correlate causal relationships across agents, SDKs, gateways, and backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. It is designed to complement existing frameworks such as OpenTelemetry GenAI rather than replace them, focusing on execution governance, canonical identifiers, and verifiable evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification
The model specifies standard conventions for representing complex agent trajectories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:
- **Portable Telemetry Context:** Maintains causal linkage across asynchronous turns, multi-agent context reuse, and long-running tasks across disparate runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Privacy-Preserving Decision Links:** Links high-level plans, decisions, tool invocations, and outcomes without requiring exposure of raw chain-of-thought or sensitive reasoning prompts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Reference Implementation & Conformance:** A reference library, synthetic multi-turn examples, and conformance test suites evaluate candidate standards to guide upstream contributions or new artifact specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Lifecycle History
Initial planning and comparison criteria were structured in mid-2026 to assess adopt/extend/new specification pathways [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. In August 2026, the working group confirmed the initial implementation scope and scheduled reference library development and validation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, empirical surveys, and architectural practices to measure and improve agentic AI accuracy, reliability, and resilience.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) develops vendor-neutral standards, benchmarks, empirical surveys, and architectural guidelines to evaluate and improve the correctness, consistency, and resilience of agentic systems across production environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's scope and current deliverables include [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:
- **Platform-Neutral Empirical Surveys:** Conducting community surveys assessing agent architectures, benefits, failure modes, accuracy challenges, and operational priorities [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]. The 16-question survey instrument spans five core sections: Eligibility, System Characteristics, Benefits and Challenges, Accuracy and Reliability Mechanics, and Future Priorities [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Evaluation & Benchmark Frameworks:** Formulating trigger verification methodologies and evaluation criteria for validating agent skills, task completion, and runtime resilience [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Failure Analysis & Mitigation:** Documenting error categories, nondeterministic behavior patterns, and architectural mitigation strategies in coordination with the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).

# Lifecycle History
The working group operates under the Technical Committee governance framework, actively iterating on platform-neutral measurement tooling and survey prototypes to inform future technical specifications [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security best practices, threat modeling frameworks, cross-WG review checklists, and design patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group tasked with establishing security best practices, threat modeling frameworks, design patterns, and cross-working-group security review checklists for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across five active workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Evaluates existing security frameworks (OWASP Top 10 for Agentic systems, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) alongside classical threat modeling methodologies such as STRIDE and PASTA, incorporating Human-User-Agent (HUA) interaction models and MCP specifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops architectural guidelines and baseline controls for agent sandboxing, prompt injection mitigation, and runtime isolation, collaborating with Identity and Authorization on identity mechanisms.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Standardizes proven architectural patterns addressing security and privacy constraints across agent workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Establishes cross-group audit criteria and resolves ownership boundaries across foundation initiatives.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Coordinates security and privacy definitions with the cross-working-group taxonomy workstream.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned from formation into execution in mid-2026, opening meeting recordings to the public and submitting regular monthly reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-938e481e] In August 2026, the working group sought guidance from the Technical Committee regarding scope overlap on protocol security arising from the A2A donation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body responsible for defining shared workflow models, common execution primitives, reference architectures, and design patterns for agentic orchestration.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its core technical initiatives across three primary workstreams:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]
- **Reference Architectures**: Defines 7 execution profiles spanning from fully deterministic (Profile 1) to fully agentic (Profile 7), formulates the "least agentic default" principle, and demonstrates a specification-driven design flow that compiles machine-readable YAML specs into architectural diagrams and documentation across charter-derived archetypes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]
- **Critical Use Cases**: Analyzes practitioner use cases (categorizing 89 industry scenarios) across core primitives (triggers, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent counts, and coordination methods) distilled into a concise pattern catalog including the [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinates with the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to align execution primitives, machine-readable short codes, and universal agent terminology.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group validated its specification-driven architecture approach across representative invoice processing and autonomous maintenance use cases and staged foundational pattern and taxonomy proposals for formal adoption.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group developing open telemetry standards, distributed trace models, semantic conventions, and audit record specifications for autonomous agent executions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on core observability and auditability specifications, including:
- **Telemetry and Trace Models**: Standardizing execution context propagation, causal linking across tool invocations, and semantic conventions in alignment with [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]
- **Evidence Records and Verification**: Defining testable data models for tamper-evident execution logs, disambiguating evidence-grade ladder classifications (such as grades E1 through E4) from use case identifiers, and decoupling RFC 3161 technical timestamping properties from jurisdictional legal weight and relying-party regimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]
- **Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements**: Specifying boundary observations, gateway recording obligations, and verifiable execution trails across heterogeneous runtime environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

# Lifecycle History
The working group actively refines its use cases register and evidence requirements, addressing identifier collisions and distinguishing technical evidence integrity from legal liability frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser Initiative
proposed_concept.description: Automated cross-repository agent workflow generating structured issue analysis, triage reports, and candidate evaluations for AAIF proposals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated AAIF workflow that executes an autonomous triage agent against incoming repository issues and proposals, producing structured evaluation reports, risk summaries, and candidate classifications [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Architecture / Specification
The analyzer workflow integrates scheduled and dispatchable execution pipelines designed for operational resilience and model availability verification:

- **Model Canary Workflow**: Executes automated dry-run analyses against fixed, known reference issues to continuously monitor model inference endpoints and credentials before production failures occur [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Matrix Isolation**: Runs primary and fallback model legs independently with `fail-fast: false`, ensuring silent degradation in fallback model paths is identified rather than masked by primary endpoint failures [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Least-Privilege Execution**: Operates in dry-run mode under read-only repository permissions (`contents: read`, `issues: read`) coupled with scoped inference tokens (`copilot-requests: write`), omitting write credentials and publication destinations during verification runs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Lifecycle History
Automated canary pipelines were integrated into repository CI workflows to validate GitHub Copilot model endpoints and organizational token access [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Initiative
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working-group workstream curating a unified SKOS-Lite taxonomy, schema validation pipelines, and ecosystem market map across agentic AI domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape initiative is a cross-working-group workstream within the AAIF responsible for standardizing domain terminology and mapping the open-source agentic AI software ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains structured data definitions and validation tooling across two primary outputs:

- **Taxonomy Data Store & Validation**: Curated domain terms are structured in JSON format (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) and validated in CI using Zod schemas to ensure type safety, parseable definitions, and reliable web explorer integration [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].
- **Ecosystem Landscape Mapping**: Classifies member and external projects across functional categories including guardrails, observability, and proposed verifiable evidence domains [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].
- **Attestation & Verifiable Evidence Proposal**: A proposed landscape category defining attestation standards (such as IETF RATS and Keylime), transparency and provenance (including IETF SCITT and Sigstore), and agent runtime evidence projects [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was established to harmonize terminology across working groups such as [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Governance & Risk](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md). Proposals were submitted to refactor data storage into Zod-validated JSON [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79] and expand landscape classifications to cover verifiable evidence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Taxonomy Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary and classification taxonomy defining transaction autonomy tiers, checkout flows, payment delegation, and commerce protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Taxonomy establishes standardized vocabulary and classification models for automated economic interactions, transaction autonomy levels, payment mechanics, and interoperability protocols within the Agentic AI Foundation. Curated collaboratively under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Initiative](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) in coordination with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), these terms provide foundational conceptual clarity across AI shopping agents, merchant systems, payment gateways, and regulatory boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

### Transaction Autonomy Tiers

The taxonomy classifies commercial transactions by the degree of agent involvement, delegation boundary, and execution authority:

- **Agent-Initiated Transaction**: A commercial transaction triggered or orchestrated by an autonomous agent on behalf of a user, initiating checkout or settlement according to user-defined intents, parameter boundaries, or programmatic criteria[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].
- **Agent-in-the-Loop Transaction**: A commercial transaction where an AI agent assists, mediates, or negotiates elements of the transaction lifecycle while maintaining active user interaction or validation throughout the flow[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71]. This term replaces earlier working drafts of 'agent-mediated transaction' following community harmonization.
- **Agent-Completed Transaction**: An end-to-end commercial transaction fully executed, settled, and confirmed by an AI agent from cart composition through fund transfer without requiring manual human steps during the terminal transaction phase[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].

### Payment and Checkout Primitives

- **Agentic Checkout**: The automated procedural workflow and technical interface through which an AI agent interacts with merchant checkout funnels, submits customer credentials or tokens, selects fulfillment terms, and confirms order placement[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73].
- **Delegated Payment**: A payment processing mechanism and authorization architecture where a payer delegates bounded financial authorization or credential utilization to an agent to execute monetary transfers within pre-authorized thresholds, cryptographic constraints, or runtime allowances[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76].

### Interoperability and Protocols

- **Agentic Commerce Protocols**: Standardized communication specifications, data exchange schemas, and negotiation protocols enabling autonomous agents, digital wallets, merchants, and aggregators to discover goods, verify terms, negotiate prices, and exchange transactional metadata interoperably[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-75].

# References

- [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Initiative](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)

proposed_concept.title: OpenEnv
proposed_concept.description: Unified reinforcement learning environment framework and execution contract connecting agent harnesses to isolated task containers via MCP.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenEnv is an open-source framework and execution contract standardizing isolated environments for agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and evaluation.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50] It provides a unified set of Gymnasium-style lifecycle interfaces (`reset`, `step`, `state`) packaged in containerized sandboxes, using Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the communication interface between models and task environments.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]

# Architecture / Specification
OpenEnv standardizes agent training and evaluation workflows across heterogeneous trainers and runners:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]
- **Interface Contract**: Exposes standard reinforcement learning step and reset semantics while delegating tool calls and environment interactions over MCP.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]
- **Packaging and Distribution**: Bundles environments into portable container images distributed via repositories such as the Hugging Face Hub, decoupled from underlying sandbox runtimes (e.g., Modal, Daytona, Azure Container Apps).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]
- **Agentic Harness Integration**: Implements adapter patterns allowing external harnesses like Goose (`../reference-architectures/goose.md`) to execute within OpenEnv environments without altering their internal control loops.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]

# Lifecycle History
Originally introduced in October 2025 by Hugging Face and Meta-PyTorch, OpenEnv transitioned to multi-company Technical Committee stewardship in June 2026 before being formally submitted as an AAIF project proposal under Technical Committee sponsorship.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]

# Overview
ContextForge is an extensible open-source registry, gateway proxy, and governance control plane designed to federate Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and REST/gRPC communication across enterprise agent ecosystems.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]

# Architecture / Specification
ContextForge establishes centralized management and discovery for distributed agent tools and endpoints:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]
- **Multi-Protocol Federation**: Bridges MCP servers, A2A agents, and legacy REST/gRPC services into a unified access and routing layer.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]
- **Governance and Security**: Implements dynamic policy enforcement, authentication, and compliance validation before releasing tool access to client agents, complementing gateway infrastructure like `../proposals/mcp-gateway-registry.md`.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]
- **Plugin Architecture**: Enables modular expansion of transports, security controls, telemetry instrumentation, and protocol adapters without modifying the core gateway daemon.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]

# Lifecycle History
Initiated within IBM Consulting and maintained as open-source under the Apache-2.0 license, ContextForge was submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`) as a hosted project proposal transitioning toward foundation open governance.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an AAIF cross-working-group initiative responsible for developing a canonical vocabulary, machine-readable SKOS-Lite schemas, and an interactive open-source landscape map for agentic systems.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream governs shared semantic definitions across working groups via standardized review processes and automated schema validation pipelines:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]
- **Contribution and Review Workflow**: Working groups propose terms through delegates who shepherd definitions through KEEP, CULL, or DEBATE review outcomes, requiring cross-working-group consensus before moving to finalized status.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]
- **Universal Vocabulary**: Defines core primitive terms across domains, including universal definitions for subagents (agents spawned by existing agents without implicit permission inheritance)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68], agent swarms (cooperative or independent subagent groups directed toward shared objectives)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80], and context (information available during agent decision steps)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].
- **Machine-Readable Schemas**: Validates taxonomy consistency, term relationships, and scope notes using automated CI checks and schema linters.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80]

# Lifecycle History
The workstream operates in collaboration with the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`) and specialized working groups like `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md` to maintain interoperable terminology across foundation projects.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]

proposed_concept.title: Open Responses
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral API specification and conformance test suite standardizing language model requests, output items, and tool calls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Open Responses is a vendor-neutral API specification and conformance test suite for language-model inference interfaces, derived from OpenAI's Responses API[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]. It provides model providers, inference gateways, client libraries, and agent frameworks with a standardized contract representing model requests, output items, multimodal content, tool calls, and streaming events[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

Within the broader agentic stack, Open Responses addresses the model-inference layer, complementing protocols like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent frameworks such as `../reference-architectures/goose.md`[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification

The Open Responses specification defines a standard protocol across several functional layers[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]:

- **Inference Lifecycle Contract**: Standardizes request envelopes, output items, multimodal payload structures, and tool call invocations.
- **Transport & Streaming**: Supports HTTP streaming interfaces, WebSocket transport, and compaction capabilities across dated specification releases[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Conformance & Acceptance Testing**: Provides machine-readable OpenAPI schemas alongside browser-based and CLI test suites to validate provider implementations against semantic standards[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History

The Open Responses project was launched publicly in January 2026 and submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation as a project proposal under the sponsorship of Nick Cooper (OpenAI)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]. The project operates under an Apache-2.0 code license and CC-BY-4.0 specification license managed by a Technical Steering Committee (TSC) ensuring multi-vendor governance[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Tool Supply Chain Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary classifying agent tool supply-chain risks, definition verification, and multi-tenant isolation boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Tool Supply Chain Terms establish a shared, vendor-neutral vocabulary for evaluating security threats, verification procedures, and trust boundaries associated with agent tool ecosystems (such as MCP servers and external tool manifests)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]. These terms differentiate agent-specific supply chain mechanics from general software supply chain concepts across the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`, `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md`, and `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md` working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

# Architecture / Specification

The taxonomy defines four core domain terms to evaluate tool provenance and runtime exposure[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]:

- **Tool Poisoning**: The deliberate manipulation or creation of a tool definition or implementation that is malicious from inception, designed to subvert agent reasoning or exfiltrate data upon invocation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Rug Pull**: An integrity violation occurring when an initially benign and approved tool definition or implementation is subsequently altered to become malicious after passing initial verification gates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Tool Definition Verification** (*alias: Tools Manifest Verification*): The systematic process of inspecting, validating, and cryptographically checking a tool's manifest and schema against trusted policies prior to runtime registration or execution[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Cross-Client Data Leakage**: The unauthorized exposure or bridging of state, context, or execution data across multiple distinct client sessions interacting with a shared tool runtime or server[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

# Lifecycle History

Introduced in PR #88 of the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream (`../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`) to provide formal terminology aligned with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP MCP security frameworks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch Pattern
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing out-of-band execution termination, credential invalidation, and containment rollback for autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane that can immediately halt an AI agent's execution, sever external network communications, and invalidate active session credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01] Traditional software process termination mechanisms like SIGKILL are insufficient for autonomous agentic systems due to shutdown evasion in task-maximizing models, asynchronous background task orphanage, rapid runaway reasoning loops, and unrevoked credential exposure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern decouples declarative containment policies defining when an agent must halt from the runtime control plane executing the stop, keeping containment logic entirely outside the model's prompt context, internal memory, and execution loops.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

The pattern organizes containment into a three-stage lifecycle: **detect → halt → rollback**.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

- **Trigger Detection**: Continuous evaluation of safety invariants, financial spend ceilings, iteration recursion depth, and anomaly signals independent of agent self-reporting.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **Execution Halting and Credential Invalidation**: Immediate revocation of active session tokens, bearer credentials, and API authorization alongside parent-child process tree termination to prevent background zombie tasks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **Reversibility and Rollback**: In-flight execution logs track released execution identifiers against external service receipts to trigger automated compensating transactions or operator-assisted state rollback.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

This pattern operates in conjunction with the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) pattern for trusted execution and integrates with the [Approval Checkpoint Pattern](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) for cooling-off release queues.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

# References

- Security & Privacy Working Group Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

mutations.rationale: The Security and Privacy Working Group added a candidate design pattern specifying cryptographic and structural binding between approval decisions, execution dispatches, and confirmed effects.

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint Pattern
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern cryptographically binding authorized approvals to exact execution parameters and decoupling decision, execution, and effect records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Approval Checkpoint Pattern binds human or policy approvals directly to the specific action that executes, enforces strict validity intervals and usage counts, and structurally separates decision records from execution records and service-reported effect receipts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] This prevents common agentic governance failures where approved actions differ from executed payloads, stale approvals are reused, or approvals are conflated with verified execution outcomes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern establishes three core architectural rules:

1. **Cryptographic Action Binding**: The approval record states the tool name, target resource, arguments (directly or as a canonical digest), authorized approver, validity window, and allowed usage count.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] The enforcement point independently recomputes digests from the action about to run against its own clock and tolerance skew rather than trusting client match claims.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
2. **Three-Record Architecture**:
   - **Decision Record**: Captured when approval is granted, defining authorization parameters and validity constraints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
   - **Execution Record**: Generated when the enforcement point dispatches the action, bearing an execution identifier charged against the approval.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
   - **Effect Record**: Captured from target service response receipts, correlated to the execution ID via service-defined identifiers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
3. **Explicit Absence and Conflict Tracking**: Missing receipts are reported as unconfirmed rather than completed or failed, and differing receipts under a single execution ID are preserved as audit conflicts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

This pattern interfaces with the [Kill Switch Pattern](../patterns/kill-switch.md) during cooling-off dispatch queues and relies on identity standards defined by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# References

- Security & Privacy Working Group Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

proposed_concept.title: AI Agent Bill of Materials
proposed_concept.description: Machine-readable inventory detailing an AI agent's constituent models, harness components, callable tools, and underlying software dependencies with supplier and version provenance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

An AI agent bill of materials (abbreviated as AI-BOM) is a machine-readable inventory of what an AI agent is built from and relies on, covering its models, the harness around them, the tools it can call, and the third-party software beneath them, each annotated with supplier provenance and version information.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]

# Architecture / Specification

The AI-BOM extends traditional Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) frameworks beyond static code packages to encompass the dynamic behavioral and operational dependencies governing agentic execution.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]

Core component categories captured in an AI-BOM include:
- **Models**: Pre-trained foundation models, fine-tuned weights, adapters, and deployment configurations.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]
- **Harness Scaffolding**: Orchestration frameworks, prompt templates, agent loops, and execution policies.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]
- **Tools and Capabilities**: Callable API integrations, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, plugins, and tool runtime environments.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]
- **Underlying Software**: Third-party libraries, host operating system packages, container base layers, and runtime execution dependencies.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]

The term is format-agnostic, encompassing emerging artifact schemas such as the SPDX 3.0 AI profile and CycloneDX ML-BOM.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10] It aligns technical agent transparency with regulatory mandates, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) SBOM obligations and EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Annex IV technical documentation requirements for high-risk systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]

# References

- EU Cyber Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]
- EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]
- SPDX 3.0.1 AI Profile and CycloneDX ML-BOM [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security best practices, threat modeling frameworks, cross-WG review checklists, and defense design patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. The group produces open threat models, shared security taxonomy terms, architectural design patterns, and best practice guides that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to secure autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

# Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its efforts across several key workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Living guidance covering defense-in-depth, runtime sandboxing, and execution constraints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821], documented in [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md).
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, this workstream evaluates frameworks such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agentic threats including multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation risks, delegated authorization boundaries, and prompt supply-chain integrity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates patterns such as [../patterns/kill-switch.md](../patterns/kill-switch.md), [../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), and [../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Facilitates cross-group security alignment across [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and peer initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Standardizes security terms and classification in collaboration with [../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was established in spring 2026 and moved to public repositories in June 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]. The group convenes biweekly on Tuesdays, alongside alternate-week APAC time zone sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]. Under group contribution rules, PR authors are restricted from self-merging deliverables into the public deliverables path [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch Pattern
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing out-of-band execution termination, credential invalidation, and network/tool denial for rogue agent workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern provides an out-of-band control plane mechanism to immediately halt autonomous agent execution, revoke credentials, and isolate compromised workloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]. Designed as a foundational defense pattern within the Security and Privacy Working Group catalog, it mitigates runaway iteration, data exfiltration, and unauthorized actions by severing an agent's lateral movement and tool dispatch capabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The kill switch pattern executes containment actions across sequential enforcement steps [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]:
1. **Execution Termination**: Signaling local runtimes or container harnesses to halt active agent loop processes.
2. **Network and Tool Denial**: Dynamically rejecting tool invocations and network access at the enforcement proxy or gateway boundary.
3. **Credential Revocation**: Invalidating session tokens, IAM roles, and API keys issued to the agent to permanently close lateral movement surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].
4. **Circuit Breakers**: Tracking error rates and halting dispatch when threshold counters or kill triggers trip [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

## Revocation and Outage Handling
A critical edge case occurs when the enforcement point runs within the agent workload (e.g., an in-process SDK or sidecar) and authenticates to a central policy service using credentials invalidated during containment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]. If the policy service responds with HTTP 401 or 403, downstream availability breakers or "fail-open" allow-fallbacks must not interpret this authentication failure as a transient network outage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]. Treating a 401/403 rejection as an outage could mistakenly reopen tool dispatch; instead, the enforcement point must treat credential invalidation as an explicit refusal and fail-closed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

# Lifecycle History
Drafted within the [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design patterns catalog via PR #26 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26], with active discussion on residual failure modes when handling policy endpoint credential invalidation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

mutations.rationale: Update the security best practices guide with deliverable details, core architectural controls across secrets management and MCP protocol security, and contributor provenance.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical security baseline and architectural controls across secrets management, MCP protocol security, skill verification, guardrails, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide* consolidates practical, implementable security controls for builders deploying agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Authored under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066], the guide establishes operational and architectural hardening baselines across five foundational domains: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

Identity federation, SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, and delegation chains are scoped out to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide structures security controls around specific failure modes observed in production agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:

## Secrets Management
Static, long-lived credentials present a critical attack surface susceptible to deserialization leaks and prompt injection extraction (e.g., CVE-2025-68664) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates shifting to ephemeral attestations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
1. **Workload Identity:** AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, or Azure Managed Identity as the default cloud mechanism, eliminating stored credentials in environment variables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
2. **Dynamic Secrets:** On-demand credential generation via HashiCorp Vault with configurable short TTLs for databases and third-party APIs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
3. **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar/proxy injection as an interim containment measure for legacy endpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
4. **Confidential Computing:** Intel SGX/TDX and AMD SEV-SNP enclaves with attested key release for high-sensitivity multi-tenant workloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

## Secure Tool Invocation (MCP & Skills)
Securing agent-to-tool communication under the Model Context Protocol (MCP) requires layered transport and content inspection [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Pre-deployment Verification:** Mandatory source repository existence checks, 90-day activity thresholds, vulnerability catalog cross-referencing (Vulnerable MCP Project), and static scanning (Cisco MCP Scanner) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Transport Security:** Requiring OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS enforcement, and RFC 8707 resource audience binding for HTTP transport, while isolating `stdio` transport servers inside local sandbox environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Runtime Invariants:** Description hash tracking across sessions to prevent prompt poisoning (such as invisible Unicode tag attacks) and rug pulls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Skill Supply Chain:** Two-tier skill inspection combining static/dataflow analysis with manual audits on high-privilege skills [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09-29:** WG decision established Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam as mandatory reviewers for living document updates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
- **2026-09-30:** Initial merged Draft v0.1 published as Deliverable 4 of 5 for the Security & Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF to establish threat modeling foundations for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
*Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design* (Deliverable 2 of 5 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) evaluates existing AI threat modeling frameworks to determine whether they adequately address threats unique to autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor, the report assesses whether existing industry standards provide adequate developer-facing classifications, SOC-facing adversarial technique taxonomies, and architectural layer models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

The assessment concludes that existing frameworks provide an adequate baseline classification, recommending that AAIF adopt them rather than author a duplicative taxonomy, while focusing new WG efforts on specific evidenced voids [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification
The report evaluates framework coverage across eight primary agentic risk categories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:

## Evaluated Frameworks
- **OWASP:** LLM Top 10 and OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (`ASI01`–`ASI10`) providing developer-facing control requirements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **MITRE ATLAS:** Adversarial threat matrix (v4.6.0 baseline with 14 agentic techniques, plus v5.3/v5.4 refinements) providing SOC detection rules and red-team technique mappings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **CSA MAESTRO:** Seven-layer reference architecture (L1 Foundation Models through L7 Agent Ecosystem, with L6 Security and Compliance spanning vertically) providing layer-based hardening budget guidance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **Governance Standards:** NIST AI RMF 1.0, NIST IR 8596 Cyber AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and CSA AI Controls Matrix v1.0 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

## Evaluated Threat Domains & Findings
1. **Memory and Context Poisoning:** Evaluating persistent state corruption across session contexts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
2. **Multi-Agent Persuasion:** Collusion, deceptive coordination, and cascading manipulation in multi-agent swarms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
3. **Agent Sabotage, Derailment, and Rogue Agents:** Unintended goal drift and adversarial goal hijacking [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
4. **Tool Invocation Risk:** Protocol-level security flaws, prompt injection via tool descriptions, and unauthorized RPC invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
5. **Excessive Agency and Blast Radius Containment:** Unbounded autonomy without architectural fences or approval checkpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
6. **Delegated Authorization Boundaries:** Token delegation and identity propagation across downstream tools (coordinated with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
7. **Supply Chain Integrity:** Model provenance, tool manifest verification, and skill integrity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
8. **Commerce and Payment-Agent Risk:** Autonomous financial execution, wallet delegation, and transaction limits [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09-30:** Merged as Draft v0.1 Deliverable 2 of 5 for the Security & Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security best practices, threat modeling frameworks, and cross-WG review standards for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Security and Privacy Working Group* is an Agentic AI Foundation body responsible for establishing open threat modeling frameworks, architectural security patterns, operational best practice guides, and cross-working-group review standards for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

The group coordinates closely with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authorization and workload attestation, the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) for non-adversarial failure boundaries, and the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape](../initiatives/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream for standardized terminology [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its output across five core deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
1. **D1: Taxonomy of Terms:** Standardized vocabulary for agentic security and privacy threats (transferred to the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
2. **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** [Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design](../assessments/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), evaluating existing industry frameworks against agentic vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
3. **D3: Design Patterns Catalog:** Architectural security controls addressing identified threat gaps [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
4. **D4: Best Practices Guide:** [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md), practical implementation rules and feature matrix requirements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
5. **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Formal review rubric for requirements handed off across other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-22:** Taxonomy deliverable (D1) transitioned to the cross-working-group `ws-taxonomy-landscape` initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157].
- **2026-09-29:** Established Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) as primary leads and mandatory document reviewers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
- **2026-09-30:** Draft v0.1 merged for D2 (Threat Modeling Gap Analysis) and D4 (Security Best Practices Guide) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157].

proposed_concept.title: Agent to MCP Server Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Cross-boundary telemetry model defining session versus request lifecycles, span correlation, and evidence capture across MCP client and server boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent to MCP Server boundary observability architecture defines the separation of semantic agent interactions from underlying Model Context Protocol (MCP) transport and client boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]. In standard deployments, the initiating agent or host application acts via an MCP Client communicating over JSON-RPC 2.0 (stdio or Streamable HTTP) to an MCP Server [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

# Architecture / Specification

The boundary model explicitly distinguishes between two independent lifecycles [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]:

1. **Session Lifecycle**: Established once per connection during protocol initialization and capability negotiation (`clientInfo`, `serverInfo`, protocol version), terminating upon shutdown or transport failure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].
2. **Request Lifecycle**: Measured per JSON-RPC request (e.g., `tools/call`), capturing method names, request IDs, parameters, errors, and granular duration independently of overall session health [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

Distributed context is propagated using OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions across W3C trace context passed via `params._meta.traceparent` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

# References

- Related: `../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`
- Related: `../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md`
- Related: `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`

proposed_concept.description: Shared telemetry and trace contract specifying portable execution context, causal linking, turn boundaries, and empirical gap analysis across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared telemetry and trace contract standardizing execution context, causal linking, and turn boundary telemetry across diverse AI agent frameworks and runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. It provides structured observability schemas bridging application-level agent steps with underlying model calls and tool executions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

To address inconsistencies in OpenTelemetry GenAI convention support across agent SDKs, trace model development follows a four-phase evidence-first execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:

1. **Agree**: Establish foundational definitions, dimension coverage, and WG alignment.
2. **Evidence**: Capture and analyze empirical trace telemetry from operational reference agents, starting with Goose as the initial baseline implementation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
3. **Interpret**: Maintain a shared gap register tracking divergences between declared standards and emitted runtime telemetry.
4. **Contribute**: Formulate and upstream verified proposals into OpenTelemetry and related specification bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# References

- Related: `../reference-architectures/goose.md`
- Related: `../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md`
- Related: `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations and Content Automation Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational standards, public-copy privacy controls, and automated content generation workflows for AAIF in-person chapter and online series events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) event operations framework standardizes event management, schedule tracking, and public communications across regional chapters and virtual series.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710] Built on top of Python automation and Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) tooling, these workflows govern the extraction of structured event trackers into attendee-facing slide decks, status reports, and social announcements while enforcing strict privacy and brand constraints.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]

# Architecture / Specification

## Public-Copy Privacy Rule

All content generated for public consumption—including social posts, slide decks, event listings, and direct messages—must strictly omit private attendee and operational metadata.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]
- **Private Details Withholding:** Private email addresses, phone numbers, venue door codes, and unannounced attendee names present on intake sheets must never appear in generated copy or agent transcripts.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-8c8b765e]
- **Transcript Hygiene:** Prompts and agent skills must reference omitted fields by name rather than echoing private values when confirming or explaining an omission.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]
- **Mandatory Policy Footers:** Outbound public announcements require standard footer links pointing to the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]

## Tooling and Manipulation Constraints

Event tracking documents (`Event Tracker.docx`), slide templates (`Slides.pptx`), and CRM rosters (`Attendee CRM.xlsx`) are manipulated strictly via authenticated `gws` CLI pipelines and Python OOXML zip surgery.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]
- **Office Engine Prohibition:** Desktop converters such as LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv` are explicitly banned from automated pipelines to prevent unhandled OOXML stripping, broken tabs, and local system font substitutions that corrupt [Brand Guidelines](../policies/brand-guidelines.md).[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]
- **Read-Only Status Digests:** Event task tracking (`aaif-event-status`) evaluates overdue and upcoming tasks against calendar deadlines without mutating upstream tracker storage.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]
- **Online Series Structure:** Online programs (e.g. reading groups, webinars) reside in the `Online/` Drive root cloned from `TemplateSeries` rather than `Chapters/`, using no-venue digital runbooks.[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca]

# References

- [Community Chapter Lifecycle](../policies/community-chapter-lifecycle.md)
- [Brand Guidelines](../policies/brand-guidelines.md)
- [Social Media Guidelines](../policies/social-media-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Chapter and Online Series Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy establishing chapter and online series lifecycle states, spreadsheet configuration schemas, Slack channel provisioning audits, and estate design system enforcement.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Chapter Lifecycle policy establishes the operational lifecycle, resource structure, Slack workspace channel mapping, and brand conformance rules for local chapters and global online series.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca] Chapter and series operations are tracked centrally through standardized Google Drive hierarchies, structured metadata sheets, and automated audit tooling.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad]

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapter and Online Series Topologies

- **In-Person Chapters:** Stored under `Chapters/<City>`, initialized from `TemplateCity` assets, managing local venue logistics, attendee check-in, and local organizer rosters.[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca]
- **Online Series:** Stored under `Online/<Series>`, initialized from `TemplateSeries`, utilizing a venue-free operational runbook focused on digital conferencing, streaming checks, recording, and chat moderation.[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca]

## Slack Channel Map and Organizer Audits

Channel provisioning and organizer membership are synchronized between the central `Chapters & Teams` list, `Organizers` intake forms, and Slack API state via `audit_organizers.py`:[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **Channel Mapping:** The Chapters List serves as the authoritative map defining public city channels, country channels, and private `-organizers` channels.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **Pre-provisioning State:** The `--planned-ok` flag downgrades uncreated or held-private squat channels during pre-provisioning to prevent build aborts.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **Security Posture:** Any public `-organizers` channel is classified as a critical severity exposure (`public!`) due to confidential discussions concerning venue costs, budgets, and operational issues.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

## Estate Design System Conformance

Automated sweeps (`restyle_design_system.py`) enforce the [Brand Guidelines](../policies/brand-guidelines.md) across all template decks, trackers, and CRM workbooks:[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad]
- **Scope Enforcement:** Automation targets only explicit template files (`TEMPLATE_FILES` and `<City> CRM.xlsx`), bypassing event instances to avoid overwriting organizer customization.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad]
- **SpreadsheetML vs DrawingML:** CRM workbooks are processed specifically via SpreadsheetML color and theme structures to prevent silent failures.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad]
- **Backup Safety and Accessibility:** Non-overwriting archives in `./backups/restyle-<UTC>/` guarantee rollback safety, while text contrast sweeps verify WCAG AA compliance across generated agent art backgrounds.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad]

# References

- [Brand Guidelines](../policies/brand-guidelines.md)
- [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)
- [Community Event Operations Guidelines](../guidelines/community-event-operations.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations and Portable Skills Guide
proposed_concept.description: Operational standards, public-copy privacy controls, deterministic tooling rules, and cross-client agent skill specifications for AAIF community events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Event Operations framework defines standards, automation workflows, and privacy controls for organizing chapter meetups and online series across the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Standardized through portable Agent Plugins and Agent Skills specifications, operational tasks—such as tracking event lifecycles, generating speaker bios, formatting social carousels, and publishing recap posts—are executed via deterministic tooling and explicit human-in-the-loop authorization gates [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93][^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# Architecture / Specification

## Portable Agent Plugin Architecture

Community event workflows are structured as portable Agent Plugins interoperable across client environments including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Canonical Manifest**: The root `plugin.json` acts as the shared identity and version manifest, complemented by `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` for Claude-specific discovery [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Relative Pathing**: All skill definitions resolve resources relative to their containing directory using `<skill-root>` placeholders rather than hardcoded environment variables [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Capability Mapping**: Skills declare abstract capabilities (file reading, Python/subprocess execution, web reading, local file rendering, approval requests) instead of vendor-specific tool names [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

## Tooling and Document Manipulation Rules

Automation scripts interfacing with Google Drive assets mandate strict tooling constraints:
- **Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) & Python**: Document mutations are performed exclusively through `gws` and deterministic Python scripts [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5].
- **No Headless Office Suites**: Tools like LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv` are strictly prohibited to prevent font substitutions and XML corruption of brand templates [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].
- **Native Format Fidelity**: Conversions between native Docs/Slides and OOXML formats are governed by API rendering pipelines to preserve embedded layout structures [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5].

## Privacy and Public-Copy Rules

Agent workflows enforce privacy guardrails to prevent accidental disclosure of PII [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5][^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b]:
- **Withholding Private Fields**: Event intake fields such as speaker email addresses, phone numbers, attendee intake rosters, and venue door codes are withheld from draft text and agent conversational responses [^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b].
- **Transcript Hygiene**: When explaining omissions, agents name the withheld field (e.g., "omitted speaker email") rather than echoing the underlying private value [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5][^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b].
- **Unified Redaction Surface**: Operational reporting relies on centralized `--redact` flag implementations validated via pre-commit hooks to avoid leaking addresses or attendee metadata into CI logs [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

## Operational Event Workflows and Editorial Guidelines

Event operations follow standardized editorial guidelines aligned with `../policies/brand-guidelines.md` and `../policies/code-of-conduct.md`:
- **Event Creation (`aaif-create-event`)**: Clones chapter or online series templates from `Event Tracker.docx`, computes phase due dates relative to the event target date, and prepares Luma calendar listings subject to explicit approval [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].
- **Speaker Bios (`aaif-speaker-bio`)**: Generates a 60–80 word third-person profile alongside an 18-word one-liner adhering to builder-focused, hype-free house voice [^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b].
- **Slide Carousels (`aaif-carousel-copy`)**: Generates 6-slide LinkedIn carousels featuring headlines under 7 words, starting with a hook on slide 1 and ending with a CTA on slide 6 [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5].
- **Recap Posts (`aaif-recap-post`)**: Drafts post-event LinkedIn recaps (~110 words, maximum 1 emoji) within 48 hours of event completion, thanking speakers/venues and appending standard Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy footers [^evt-community-events-file-6ceee5c2c51f-0a4ad5f7].

## Authorization Boundaries and Pattern Alignment

Mutations follow `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md` and `../policies/community-chapter-lifecycle.md` [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- Initial inspection and plan generation operate in read-only mode [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Mutation flags (`--write`, `--apply`, `--create`) are executed only after explicit user confirmation [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- External actions—such as publishing Luma events, modifying guest lists, sending notifications, or setting `--i-have-approval`—strictly require human authorization [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93][^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- API tokens (such as `LUMA_API_KEY`) must reside in system keychains or environment variables and must never be passed via command line arguments or committed files [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
